original: Namo tassa Bhagavato Arahato Sammāsambuddhassa.
text: Homage to him, the blessed one, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!
title: Akitti’s Conduct (Akitticariya)

original:
“Kappe ca satasahasse,
caturo ca asaṅkhiye;
Etthantare yaṁ caritaṁ,
sabbaṁ taṁ bodhipācanaṁ.
text:
“For a hundred thousand eons
and four incalculable ages,
all my conduct in that period
ripens in awakening.

original:
Atītakappe caritaṁ,
ṭhapayitvā bhavābhave;
Imamhi kappe caritaṁ,
pavakkhissaṁ suṇohi me.
text:
Setting aside my conduct
in past eons through different lives,
I shall speak of my conduct
in this eon, hear me.

original:
Yadā ahaṁ brahāraññe,
suññe vipinakānane;
Ajjhogāhetvā viharāmi,
akitti nāma tāpaso.
text:
When I lived having plunged
into the formidable jungle
of empty thickets and glades,
my name was Akitti the mortifier.

original:
Tadā maṁ tapatejena,
santatto tidivābhibhū;
Dhārento brāhmaṇavaṇṇaṁ,
bhikkhāya maṁ upāgami.
text:
Then, burned by the fires of my mortification,
the sovereign of the Third Heaven,
came to me for alms
in the form of a brahmin.

original:
Pavanā ābhataṁ paṇṇaṁ,
atelañca aloṇikaṁ;
Mama dvāre ṭhitaṁ disvā,
sakaṭāhena ākiriṁ.
text:
I had gathered leaves from the forest
without oil or salt,
and seeing him standing at my door,
I placed them in his pot.

original:
Tassa datvānahaṁ paṇṇaṁ,
nikkujjitvāna bhājanaṁ;
Punesanaṁ jahitvāna,
pāvisiṁ paṇṇasālakaṁ.
text:
After giving him the leaves
I turned over my plate,
and having given up on seeking more food,
I entered my hut of leaves.

original:
Dutiyampi tatiyampi,
upagañchi mamantikaṁ;
Akampito anolaggo,
evamevamadāsahaṁ.
text:
A second and a third time
he came to me.
Undisturbed, ungrasping,
I gave in just the same way.

original:
Na me tappaccayā atthi,
sarīrasmiṁ vivaṇṇiyaṁ;
Pītisukhena ratiyā,
vītināmemi taṁ divaṁ.
text:
That is the reason why
my body is not discolored.
In rapture and bliss free of relishing
I spend the day.

original:
Yadi māsampi dvemāsaṁ,
dakkhiṇeyyaṁ varaṁ labhe;
Akampito anolīno,
dadeyyaṁ dānamuttamaṁ.
text:
If even for a month or two
I were to find a worthy recipient,
undisturbed, unattached,
I would give the supreme gift.

original:
Na tassa dānaṁ dadamāno,
yasaṁ lābhañca patthayiṁ;
Sabbaññutaṁ patthayāno,
tāni kammāni ācarin”ti.
text:
While giving him that gift
I did not wish for fame or profit.
Wishing for omniscience
I performed those deeds.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
Brāhmaṇo saṅkhasavhayo;
Mahāsamuddaṁ taritukāmo,
Upagacchāmi paṭṭanaṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
a brahmin named Saṅkha,
wanting to cross the great ocean,
I was on my way to the port.
title: Saṅkha’s Conduct (Saṅkhacariya)

original:
Tatthaddasaṁ paṭipathe,
Sayambhuṁ aparājitaṁ;
Kantāraddhānaṁ paṭipannaṁ,
Tattāya kaṭhinabhūmiyā.
text:
There I saw across the way
one self-awakened, undefeated,
walking a desert road
whose ground was hot and rough.

original:
Tamahaṁ paṭipathe disvā,
imamatthaṁ vicintayiṁ;
‘Idaṁ khettaṁ anuppattaṁ,
puññakāmassa jantuno.
text:
Seeing him across the way,
I thought this:
‘A field has appeared
for a personage desiring merit.

original:
Yathā kassako puriso,
khettaṁ disvā mahāgamaṁ;
Tattha bījaṁ na ropeti,
na so dhaññena atthiko.
text:
Now suppose a farmer
seeing a fertile field
does not sow seed there,
then they are not in need of grain.

original:
Evamevāhaṁ puññakāmo,
Disvā khettavaruttamaṁ;
Yadi tattha kāraṁ na karomi,
Nāhaṁ puññena atthiko.
text:
So too, if I, desiring merit,
seeing a supreme excellent field,
do not render service there,
then I am not in need of merit.

original:
Yathā amacco muddikāmo,
rañño antepure jane;
Na deti tesaṁ dhanadhaññaṁ,
muddito parihāyati.
text:
Or suppose a minister seeking the royal seal
of authority over the people of the court,
does not give them money and grain,
their authority dwindles.

original:
Evamevāhaṁ puññakāmo,
Vipulaṁ disvāna dakkhiṇaṁ;
Yadi tassa dānaṁ na dadāmi,
Parihāyissāmi puññato’.
text:
So too, if I, desiring merit,
seeing an abundantly worthy recipient,
do not give gifts to them,
I will dwindle in merit.’

original:
Evāhaṁ cintayitvāna,
orohitvā upāhanā;
Tassa pādāni vanditvā,
adāsiṁ chattupāhanaṁ.
text:
Reflecting in this way,
I took off my sandals
and bowed to his feet,
giving him an umbrella and sandals.

original:
Tenevāhaṁ sataguṇato,
Sukhumālo sukhedhito;
Api ca dānaṁ paripūrento,
Evaṁ tassa adāsahan”ti.
text:
Though I was a hundred times
more delicate and pampered than him,
fulfilling my giving,
I gave like this to him.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
indapatthe puruttame;
Rājā dhanañcayo nāma,
kusale dasahupāgato.
text:
“Then again when I reigned
in Indapatta, the capital city,
as the king named Dhanañjaya
I was blessed with the ten skillful deeds.
title: Kururāja’s Conduct (Kururājacariya)

original:
Kaliṅgaraṭṭhavisayā,
brāhmaṇā upagañchu maṁ;
Āyācuṁ maṁ hatthināgaṁ,
dhaññaṁ maṅgalasammataṁ.
text:
From the realm of Kaliṅga
brahmins came to me
requesting the royal elephant
that was lucky and deemed auspicious.

original:
‘Avuṭṭhiko janapado,
dubbhikkho chātako mahā;
Dadāhi pavaraṁ nāgaṁ,
nīlaṁ añjanasavhayaṁ’.
text:
‘Our nation is suffering from drought,
food is scarce and famine abounds,
please give the noble elephant
of midnight hue named Añjana.’

original:
‘Na me yācakamanuppatte,
paṭikkhepo anucchavo;
Mā me bhijji samādānaṁ,
dassāmi vipulaṁ gajaṁ’.
text:
‘When supplicants come to me
it is unbefitting to refuse.
Let not my vow be broken,
I shall give the mighty elephant.’

original:
Nāgaṁ gahetvā soṇḍāya,
bhiṅgāre ratanāmaye;
Jalaṁ hatthe ākiritvā,
brāhmaṇānaṁ adaṁ gajaṁ.
text:
Taking the elephant by the trunk,
and a bejeweled ceremonial vessel,
I sprinkled water on the hand,
and gave the elephant to the brahmins.

original:
Tassa nāge padinnamhi,
amaccā etadabravuṁ;
‘Kiṁ nu tuyhaṁ varaṁ nāgaṁ,
yācakānaṁ padassasi.
text:
When I had given the elephant,
my ministers said,
‘Why did you give the noble elephant
to the supplicants?

original:
Dhaññaṁ maṅgalasampannaṁ,
saṅgāmavijayuttamaṁ;
Tasmiṁ nāge padinnamhi,
kiṁ te rajjaṁ karissati’.
text:
He was lucky and endowed with the auspicious,
supreme victor in battle.
Now you have given the elephant,
how shall you govern the realm?’

original:
‘Rajjampi me dade sabbaṁ,
sarīraṁ dajjamattano;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā nāgaṁ adāsahan’”ti.
text:
‘I would give the entire realm
and my physical body as well.
Omniscience is precious to me,
which is why I gave away the elephant.’”

original:
“Kusāvatimhi nagare,
yadā āsiṁ mahīpati;
Mahāsudassano nāma,
cakkavattī mahabbalo.
text:
“In the city of Kusāvatī,
when I was Lord of the Earth,
my name was Sudassana the Great,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
title: Mahāsudassana’s Conduct (Mahāsudassanacariya)

original:
Tatthāhaṁ divase tikkhattuṁ,
ghosāpemi tahiṁ tahiṁ;
‘Ko kiṁ icchati pattheti,
kassa kiṁ dīyatū dhanaṁ.
text:
There, thrice a day,
I declared in one place or another:
‘Who needs what? Who wants what?
To whom ought riches be given?

original:
Ko chātako ko tasito,
ko mālaṁ ko vilepanaṁ;
Nānārattāni vatthāni,
ko naggo paridahissati.
text:
Who needs an umbrella? Who is thirsty?
Who a garland? Who some makeup?
What person, being naked,
and will put on colorful clothes?

original:
Ko pathe chattamādeti,
kopāhanā mudū subhā’;
Iti sāyañca pāto ca,
ghosāpemi tahiṁ tahiṁ.
text:
Who will take an umbrella on a highway,
who needs sandals, soft and pretty?’
Thus I had it proclaimed everywhere
morning and night.

original:
Na taṁ dasasu ṭhānesu,
napi ṭhānasatesu vā;
Anekasataṭhānesu,
paṭiyattaṁ yācake dhanaṁ.
text:
It was not just in ten places,
or even a hundred,
but in many hundreds of places
riches were prepared for supplicants.

original:
Divā vā yadi vā rattiṁ,
yadi eti vanibbako;
Laddhā yadicchakaṁ bhogaṁ,
pūrahatthova gacchati.
text:
By day or by night
if a supplicant comes,
then having gotten all he wants,
he leaves with full hands.

original:
Evarūpaṁ mahādānaṁ,
Adāsiṁ yāvajīvikaṁ;
Napāhaṁ dessaṁ dhanaṁ dammi,
Napi natthi nicayo mayi.
text:
I gave great gifts like this
for my whole life.
I did not give because I disliked riches,
or because I had a store set aside.

original:
Yathāpi āturo nāma,
rogato parimuttiyā;
Dhanena vejjaṁ tappetvā,
rogato parimuccati.
text:
Suppose a person is sick.
In order to be free of sickness
having compensated the doctor with money,
they become freed from sickness.

Thus I, knowingly,
in order to fulfill without remainder,
to fulfill what is lacking,
gave gifts to supplicants
without clinging or reward,
for the attainment of awakening.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
sattarājapurohito;
Pūjito naradevehi,
mahāgovindabrāhmaṇo.
text:
“Then again when I was
high priest for seven kings,
I was venerated by the gods among men
as the brahmin Mahāgovinda.
title: Mahāgovinda’s Conduct (Mahāgovindacariya)

original:
Tadāhaṁ sattarajjesu,
Yaṁ me āsi upāyanaṁ;
Tena demi mahādānaṁ,
Akkhobbhaṁ sāgarūpamaṁ.
text:
Then in all seven kingdoms
what I received as tribute
I used to give a great gift
unwavering as the ocean.

original:
Na me dessaṁ dhanaṁ dhaññaṁ,
Napi natthi nicayo mayi;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
Tasmā demi varaṁ dhanan”ti.
text:
It was not because I disliked riches or grain,
or because I had a store set aside,
but because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I gave such fine riches.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
mithilāyaṁ puruttame;
Nimi nāma mahārājā,
paṇḍito kusalatthiko.
text:
“Then again when I was
in the capital city of Mithilā
I was the great king named Nimi,
astute and seeking the good.
title: King Nimi’s Conduct (Nimirājacariya)

original:
Tadāhaṁ māpayitvāna,
catussālaṁ catummukhaṁ;
Tattha dānaṁ pavattesiṁ,
migapakkhinarādinaṁ.
text:
Then having had constructed
four halls with four openings,
I provided gifts there
for beasts, birds, men, and so forth.

original:
Acchādanañca sayanaṁ,
annaṁ pānañca bhojanaṁ;
Abbocchinnaṁ karitvāna,
mahādānaṁ pavattayiṁ.
text:
Clothing and beds,
food and drink to enjoy:
I provided them without let,
performing a great offering.

original:
Yathāpi sevako sāmiṁ,
dhanahetumupāgato;
Kāyena vācā manasā,
ārādhanīyamesati.
text:
Suppose a servant is looking
to get a raise from their boss,
they’d seek to fulfill their needs
by body, speech, and mind.

original:
Tathevāhaṁ sabbabhave,
pariyesissāmi bodhijaṁ;
Dānena satte tappetvā,
icchāmi bodhimuttaman”ti.
text:
In that way in every life
I shall seek the wisdom born of awakening.
Having pleased beings with gifts,
I wish for the supreme awakening.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
ekarājassa atrajo;
Nagare pupphavatiyā,
kumāro candasavhayo.
text:
“Then again when I was
the true-born son of the One King
in the city of flowers, Pupphavatī,
I was called Prince Canda, the Moon.
title: Prince Candana’s Conduct (Candakumāracariya)

original:
Tadāhaṁ yajanā mutto,
nikkhanto yaññavāṭato;
Saṁvegaṁ janayitvāna,
mahādānaṁ pavattayiṁ.
text:
Then, released from being sacrificed,
I fled the sacrificial enclosure.
Giving rise to a sense of urgency,
I performed a great offering.

original:
Nāhaṁ pivāmi khādāmi,
napi bhuñjāmi bhojanaṁ;
Dakkhiṇeyye adatvāna,
api chappañcarattiyo.
text:
I did not drink, I did not eat,
I did not enjoy any food
for five or six days
without offering to a worthy recipient.

original:
Yathāpi vāṇijo nāma,
Katvāna bhaṇḍasañcayaṁ;
Yattha lābho mahā hoti,
Tattha taṁ harati bhaṇḍakaṁ.
text:
Suppose there was a merchant
who had made a store of goods.
They would take those goods
to where they could make a large profit.

original:
Tatheva sakabhuttāpi,
pare dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ;
Tasmā parassa dātabbaṁ,
satabhāgo bhavissati.
text:
So too, even giving what one has used oneself
to others is very fruitful.
That is why what is to be given to others
multiplies a hundredfold.

original:
Etamatthavasaṁ ñatvā,
demi dānaṁ bhavābhave;
Na paṭikkamāmi dānato,
sambodhimanupattiyā”ti.
text:
Knowing the reason for this,
I gave gifts in life after life.
Aiming for awakening,
I never backtracked from giving.”

original:
“Ariṭṭhasavhaye nagare,
sivināmāsi khattiyo;
Nisajja pāsādavare,
evaṁ cintesahaṁ tadā.
text:
“In the city called Ariṭṭha
I was the aristocrat named Sivi.
Seated in my finest longhouse,
I then had the following thought:
title: King Sivi’s Conduct (Sivirājacariya)

original:
‘Yaṁ kiñci mānusaṁ dānaṁ,
adinnaṁ me na vijjati;
Yopi yāceyya maṁ cakkhuṁ,
dadeyyaṁ avikampito’.
text:
‘Whatever human gifts there are,
none may be found that I have not given.
Even if someone were to ask for my eye,
I would give it without wavering.’

original:
Mama saṅkappamaññāya,
sakko devānamissaro;
Nisinno devaparisāya,
idaṁ vacanamabravi.
text:
Knowing my thoughts,
Sakka the lord of gods,
sitting in the assembly of gods
said the following.

original:
‘Nisajja pāsādavare,
sivirājā mahiddhiko;
Cintento vividhaṁ dānaṁ,
adeyyaṁ so na passati.
text:
‘Seated in his finest longhouse,
the mighty King Sivi
is thinking of manifold gifts
and cannot see any he would not give.

original:
Tathaṁ nu vitathaṁ netaṁ,
handa vīmaṁsayāmi taṁ;
Muhuttaṁ āgameyyātha,
yāva jānāmi taṁ manaṁ’.
text:
Is this true or not?
Come, let us test him.
Wait a while
until I know his mind.’

original:
Pavedhamāno palitasiro,
Valigatto jarāturo;
Andhavaṇṇova hutvāna,
Rājānaṁ upasaṅkami.
text:
Appearing as a frail old man,
with grey hair and wrinkled skin,
feeble and blind,
he approached the king.

original:
So tadā paggahetvāna,
vāmaṁ dakkhiṇabāhu ca;
Sirasmiṁ añjaliṁ katvā,
idaṁ vacanamabravi.
text:
Then, stretching out
his left and right arms,
he raised his cupped palms to his head
and said the following.

original:
‘Yācāmi taṁ mahārāja,
dhammika raṭṭhavaḍḍhana;
Tava dānaratā kitti,
uggatā devamānuse.
text:
‘Great king, I have a request for you.
Under your just rule the kingdom has flourished,
and the renown of your love of giving
has risen among gods and humans.

original:
Ubhopi nettā nayanā,
andhā upahatā mama;
Ekaṁ me nayanaṁ dehi,
tvampi ekena yāpaya’.
text:
Both my eyes, by which I find my way,
are ruined and become blind.
Give me just one eye,
while you too get by with one.’

original:
Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
haṭṭho saṁviggamānaso;
Katañjalī vedajāto,
idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ.
text:
After hearing his words
I was thrilled, my mind elated,
so with cupped palms, inspired,
I said the following.

original:
‘Idānāhaṁ cintayitvāna,
pāsādato idhāgato;
Tvaṁ mama cittamaññāya,
nettaṁ yācitumāgato.
text:
‘Just now I was reflecting on this
when I came here from the longhouse.
Understanding my mind,
you have come to ask for an eye.

original:
Aho me mānasaṁ siddhaṁ,
saṅkappo paripūrito;
Adinnapubbaṁ dānavaraṁ,
ajja dassāmi yācake.
text:
Oh! My wish has come true!
My intention is fulfilled!
Today I shall give to a supplicant
a fine gift never before given.’

original:
Ehi sivaka uṭṭhehi,
mā dandhayi mā pavedhayi;
Ubhopi nayanaṁ dehi,
uppāṭetvā vaṇibbake’.
text:
‘Come Sivaka, stand up,
do not hesitate or waver.
Pluck out even both eyes
and give them to the supplicant.’

original:
Tato so codito mayhaṁ,
sivako vacanaṁ karo;
Uddharitvāna pādāsi,
tālamiñjaṁva yācake.
text:
And then, urged on by me,
Sivaka did as I said.
Extracting both eyes,
he presented them to the trembling supplicant.

original:
Dadamānassa dentassa,
dinnadānassa me sato;
Cittassa aññathā natthi,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā.
text:
‘While planning to give, while giving,
and after I had given,
my mind did not falter,
because it was solely for awakening.

original:
Na me dessā ubho cakkhū,
attā na me na dessiyo;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā cakkhuṁ adāsahan”ti.
text:
It was not because I disliked my eyes,
or that I disliked myself,
but because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I gave away my eyes.’”

original:
“Yā me ahosi janikā,
phussatī nāma khattiyā;
Sā atītāsu jātīsu,
sakkassa mahesī piyā.
text:
“She who was my mother,
the aristocrat lady named Phussatī,
was Sakka’s beloved queen
in past lives.
title: Vessantara’s Conduct (Vessantaracariya)

original:
Tassā āyukkhayaṁ ñatvā,
devindo etadabravi;
‘Dadāmi te dasa vare,
varabhadde yadicchasi’.
text:
Knowing that she was at the end of life,
the lord of gods said this:
‘I grant you ten favors,
my dear, whatever favor you wish.’

When he said this the queen
replied to Sakka:
‘In what way am I deficient?
How am I displeasing to you?
You send me from this lovely place,
like the wind a feeble tree.’

original:
Evaṁ vutto ca so sakko,
puna tassidamabravi;
‘Na ceva te kataṁ pāpaṁ,
na ca me tvaṁsi appiyā.
text:
When she said this Sakka
replied to her:
‘You have done nothing wrong,
nor are you not beloved to me.

original:
Ettakaṁyeva te āyu,
cavanakālo bhavissati;
Paṭiggaṇha mayā dinne,
vare dasa varuttame’.
text:
But your life lasts only so long,
your time of death will come.
Accept the ten supreme favors
I offer to you.’

original:
Sakkena sā dinnavarā,
tuṭṭhahaṭṭhā pamoditā;
Mamaṁ abbhantaraṁ katvā,
phussatī dasa vare varī.
text:
She accepted the offerings of Sakka,
full of joy and happiness.
Having conceived me,
Phussatī was blessed with the ten favors.

original:
Tato cutā sā phussatī,
khattiye upapajjatha;
Jetuttaramhi nagare,
sañjayena samāgami.
text:
Then Phussatī, having passed from there,
was reborn as an aristocrat
in the city of Jetuttara,
where she married Sañjaya.

original:
Yadāhaṁ phussatiyā kucchiṁ,
okkanto piyamātuyā;
Mama tejena me mātā,
sadā dānaratā ahu.
text:
Once I was conceived in the womb
of my dear mother Phussatī,
because of my power,
my mother always delighted in giving.

original:
Adhane āture jiṇṇe,
yācake addhike jane;
Samaṇe brāhmaṇe khīṇe,
deti dānaṁ akiñcane.
text:
She gave to the destitute, the ailing and aging,
to beggars, travelers, and folk,
to ascetics and brahmins, and the dispossessed,
and to those who had nothing.

original:
Dasa māse dhārayitvāna,
karonte puraṁ padakkhiṇaṁ;
Vessānaṁ vīthiyā majjhe,
janesi phussatī mamaṁ.
text:
Having carried me for ten months,
she was proceeding around the city
when Phussatī gave birth to me
in the middle of the peasant’s street.

original:
Na mayhaṁ mattikaṁ nāmaṁ,
napi pettikasambhavaṁ;
Jātettha vessavīthiyā,
tasmā vessantaro ahu.
text:
My name was not from my mother’s side,
nor from my father’s.
I was born there in the peasant’s street,
and that’s why I’m called Vessantara.

original:
Yadāhaṁ dārako homi,
jātiyā aṭṭhavassiko;
Tadā nisajja pāsāde,
dānaṁ dātuṁ vicintayiṁ.
text:
When I was a boy
of only eight years old,
sitting in the stilt longhouse,
I thought of giving gifts.

original:
‘Hadayaṁ dadeyyaṁ cakkhuṁ,
maṁsampi rudhirampi ca;
Dadeyyaṁ kāyaṁ sāvetvā,
yadi koci yācaye mamaṁ’.
text:
‘I would give my heart and my eyes,
my flesh and blood too.’
I announced that I would give my body,
if anyone asked me.

original:
Sabhāvaṁ cintayantassa,
akampitamasaṇṭhitaṁ;
Akampi tattha pathavī,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
Reflecting on my state of mind,
so undisturbed and steadfast,
the earth quaked there,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Anvaddhamāse pannarase,
puṇṇamāse uposathe;
Paccayaṁ nāgamāruyha,
dānaṁ dātuṁ upāgamiṁ.
text:
Every fortnight, the fifteenth,
and the sabbath when the moon was full,
I mounted the tusker Paccaya
and went to give gifts.

original:
Kaliṅgaraṭṭhavisayā,
brāhmaṇā upagañchu maṁ;
Ayācuṁ maṁ hatthināgaṁ,
dhaññaṁ maṅgalasammataṁ.
text:
From the country of Kaliṅga,
the brahmins came to me,
requesting the royal elephant,
that was lucky and deemed as auspicious.

original:
‘Avuṭṭhiko janapado,
dubbhikkho chātako mahā;
Dadāhi pavaraṁ nāgaṁ,
sabbasetaṁ gajuttamaṁ’.
text:
‘Our nation is suffering from drought,
food is scarce and famine abounds,
please give the noble elephant
the all-white supreme elephant.’

original:
Dadāmi na vikampāmi,
yaṁ maṁ yācanti brāhmaṇā;
Santaṁ nappatigūhāmi,
dāne me ramate mano.
text:
‘I give without hesitation
what you ask of me, brahmins.
I do not hide what I have,
for my heart is happy to give.

original:
Na me yācakamanuppatte,
paṭikkhepo anucchavo;
Mā me bhijji samādānaṁ,
dassāmi vipulaṁ gajaṁ.
text:
When supplicants come to me
it is unbefitting to refuse.
Let not my vow be broken,
I shall give the mighty elephant.’

original:
Nāgaṁ gahetvā soṇḍāya,
bhiṅgāre ratanāmaye;
Jalaṁ hatthe ākiritvā,
brāhmaṇānaṁ adaṁ gajaṁ.
text:
Taking the elephant by the trunk,
and a bejeweled ceremonial vessel,
I sprinkled water on the hand,
and gave the elephant to the brahmins.

original:
Punāparaṁ dadantassa,
sabbasetaṁ gajuttamaṁ;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
Then again when I was giving
the all-white supreme elephant,
the earth quaked again,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Tassa nāgassa dānena,
sivayo kuddhā samāgatā;
Pabbājesuṁ sakā raṭṭhā,
‘vaṅkaṁ gacchatu pabbataṁ’.
text:
At the gift of the tusker,
angry Sivian folk gathered
and banished me from my kingdom, saying:
‘Go to Crooked Mountain.’

original:
Tesaṁ nicchubhamānānaṁ,
akampitamasaṇṭhitaṁ;
Mahādānaṁ pavattetuṁ,
ekaṁ varamayācisaṁ.
text:
While they were ejecting me,
I was undisturbed and steadfast,
I asked one favor:
to perform a great offering.

original:
Yācitā sivayo sabbe,
ekaṁ varamadaṁsu me;
Sāvayitvā kaṇṇabheriṁ,
mahādānaṁ dadāmahaṁ.
text:
When I asked, all the Sivian folk
granted me that one favor.
Sounding the drums,
I gave a great offering.

original:
Athettha vattatī saddo,
tumulo bheravo mahā;
Dānenimaṁ nīharanti,
puna dānaṁ dadātayaṁ.
text:
And as the sound went forth,
there was a great tumult and upset.
They drove me out because of giving,
but I just gave again.

original:
Hatthiṁ asse rathe datvā,
dāsiṁ dāsaṁ gavaṁ dhanaṁ;
Mahādānaṁ daditvāna,
nagarā nikkhamiṁ tadā.
text:
Elephants, horses, chariots,
male and female slaves, cattle, and riches:
after giving this great gift
I then left the city.

original:
Nikkhamitvāna nagarā,
nivattitvā vilokite;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
After leaving the city,
I turned back to look,
at which the earth quaked,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Catuvāhiṁ rathaṁ datvā,
ṭhatvā cātummahāpathe;
Ekākiyo adutiyo,
maddideviṁ idamabraviṁ.
text:
Having given away my four-horse chariot,
I was standing at the crossroads
alone with no partner,
and I said to Queen Maddī:

original:
‘Tvaṁ maddi kaṇhaṁ gaṇhāhi,
lahukā esā kaniṭṭhikā;
Ahaṁ jāliṁ gahessāmi,
garuko bhātiko hi so’.
text:
‘Maddī, you take Kaṇhā,
for she, as the younger sister, is the lighter.
I shall take Jāli,
for he, as the brother, is heavier.’

original:
Padumaṁ puṇḍarīkaṁva,
maddī kaṇhājinaggahī;
Ahaṁ suvaṇṇabimbaṁva,
jāliṁ khattiyamaggahiṁ.
text:
Like a pink or white lotus,
Maddī picked up Kaṇhājinā.
Like a golden statue,
I picked up Jāli, the aristocrat.

original:
Abhijātā sukhumālā,
khattiyā caturo janā;
Visamaṁ samaṁ akkamantā,
vaṅkaṁ gacchāma pabbataṁ.
text:
High-born and delicate,
four aristocrat folk
traveled ground even and uneven,
going to Crooked Mountain.

original:
Ye keci manujā enti,
anumagge paṭippathe;
Maggante paṭipucchāma,
‘kuhiṁ vaṅkantapabbato’.
text:
Whenever men would come along,
coming the other way along the road,
we asked them in the middle of the street,
‘Where is Crooked Mountain?’

original:
Te tattha amhe passitvā,
karuṇaṁ giramudīrayuṁ;
Dukkhante paṭivedenti,
dūre vaṅkantapabbato.
text:
Seeing us there,
they spoke to us kindly,
‘It will be hard for you,’ they explained,
‘for Crooked Mountain is far.’

original:
Yadi passanti pavane,
dārakā phaline dume;
Tesaṁ phalānaṁ hetumhi,
uparodanti dārakā.
text:
If the children saw fruit
on a tree in the forest,
then for the sake of that fruit,
the children cried.

original:
Rodante dārake disvā,
ubbiddhā vipulā dumā;
Sayamevoṇamitvāna,
upagacchanti dārake.
text:
Seeing the children cry,
the tall, massive trees
bent down of their own accord,
within reach of the children.

original:
Idaṁ acchariyaṁ disvā,
abbhutaṁ lomahaṁsanaṁ;
Sāhukāraṁ pavattesi,
maddī sabbaṅgasobhanā.
text:
Seeing this marvel,
so astonishing and hair-raising,
Maddī, beautiful in every limb,
exclaimed in celebration:

original:
Accheraṁ vata lokasmiṁ,
abbhutaṁ lomahaṁsanaṁ;
Vessantarassa tejena,
sayamevoṇatā dumā.
text:
‘Such a marvel in the world,
so astonishing and hair-raising,
due to the power of Vessantara,
the trees bent down of their own accord.’

original:
Saṅkhipiṁsu pathaṁ yakkhā,
anukampāya dārake;
Nikkhantadivaseneva,
cetaraṭṭhamupāgamuṁ.
text:
Native spirits, out of compassion,
shortened the path,
so that on the very day they set out,
they arrived at the kingdom of Ceta.

original:
Saṭṭhirājasahassāni,
tadā vasanti mātule;
Sabbe pañjalikā hutvā,
rodamānā upāgamuṁ.
text:
Sixty thousand kings
were living at Mātula then.
All raised their cupped palms,
and approached, weeping.

original:
Tattha vattetvā sallāpaṁ,
cetehi cetaputtehi;
Te tato nikkhamitvāna,
vaṅkaṁ agamu pabbataṁ.
text:
There they held conversation
with the folks of Ceta and their children.
Then, leaving that place,
they arrived at Crooked Mountain.

original:
Āmantayitvā devindo,
vissakammaṁ mahiddhikaṁ;
Assamaṁ sukataṁ rammaṁ,
paṇṇasālaṁ sumāpaya.
text:
The lord of gods addressed
Vissakamma of great psychic power:
‘Build a hermitage, well-made and delightful,
with a hall of leaves.’

original:
Sakkassa vacanaṁ sutvā,
vissakammo mahiddhiko;
Assamaṁ sukataṁ rammaṁ,
paṇṇasālaṁ sumāpayi.
text:
After hearing Sakka’s words,
Vissakamma of great psychic power
built a hermitage, well-made and delightful,
with a hall of leaves.

original:
Ajjhogāhetvā pavanaṁ,
appasaddaṁ nirākulaṁ;
Caturo janā mayaṁ tattha,
vasāma pabbatantare.
text:
Having plunged into the forest,
quiet and undisturbed,
we four persons
lived there in the mountains.

original:
Ahañca maddidevī ca,
jālī kaṇhājinā cubho;
Aññamaññaṁ sokanudā,
vasāma assame tadā.
text:
Myself and Queen Maddī,
with both Jāli and Kaṇhājinā,
dispelling each other’s sorrow
lived then in that hermitage.

original:
Dārake anurakkhanto,
asuñño homi assame;
Maddī phalaṁ āharitvā,
poseti sā tayo jane.
text:
While caring for the children,
I was not idle in the hermitage.
Maddī gathered fruit,
and provided for three people.

original:
Pavane vasamānassa,
addhiko maṁ upāgami;
Āyāci puttake mayhaṁ,
jāliṁ kaṇhājinaṁ cubho.
text:
While I was living in the forest,
a traveler came to me
and asked for my children,
both Jāli and Kaṇhājinā.

original:
Yācakaṁ upagataṁ disvā,
hāso me upapajjatha;
Ubho putte gahetvāna,
adāsiṁ brāhmaṇe tadā.
text:
When I saw the supplicant approaching,
I felt so full of joy.
Taking both my children,
I gave them to the brahmin then.

original:
Sake putte cajantassa,
jūjake brāhmaṇe yadā;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
When I gave away my own children,
to the brahmin Jūjaka,
the earth quaked again,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Punadeva sakko oruyha,
hutvā brāhmaṇasannibho;
Āyāci maṁ maddideviṁ,
sīlavantiṁ patibbataṁ.
text:
And then Sakka descended
in the guise of a brahmin.
He asked me for Queen Maddī,
virtuous, and devoted.

original:
Maddiṁ hatthe gahetvāna,
udakañjali pūriya;
Pasannamanasaṅkappo,
tassa maddiṁ adāsahaṁ.
text:
Taking Maddī by the hand,
filling clasped hands with water,
with a confident heart,
I gave Maddī to him.

original:
Maddiyā dīyamānāya,
gagane devā pamoditā;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
As Maddī was being given,
gods applauded in the welkin,
and the earth quaked again,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Jāliṁ kaṇhājinaṁ dhītaṁ,
maddideviṁ patibbataṁ;
Cajamāno na cintesiṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā.
text:
Jāli and Kaṇhājinā my daughter,
and Queen Maddī my devoted wife:
I gave them up without a second thought,
because it was solely for awakening.

original:
Na me dessā ubho puttā,
maddidevī na dessiyā;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā piye adāsahaṁ.
text:
I had no dislike of my children,
nor for Queen Maddī.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
I gave my loved ones away.

original:
Punāparaṁ brahāraññe,
mātāpitusamāgame;
Karuṇaṁ paridevante,
sallapante sukhaṁ dukhaṁ.
text:
Later on in the mighty forest,
we were reunited by my mother and father.
Crying pitifully,
they spoke of my happiness and sadness.

original:
Hirottappena garunā,
ubhinnaṁ upasaṅkami;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
With deep conscience and prudence,
I approached them,
at which the earth quaked,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Punāparaṁ brahāraññā,
nikkhamitvā sañātibhi;
Pavisāmi puraṁ rammaṁ,
jetuttaraṁ puruttamaṁ.
text:
Later on in the mighty forest,
having left the forest with my family,
I entered the delightful city
Jetuttara, the capital city.

original:
Ratanāni satta vassiṁsu,
mahāmegho pavassatha;
Tadāpi pathavī kampi,
sineruvanavaṭaṁsakā.
text:
The seven gems rained down,
raining forth from a mighty cloud,
and the earth quaked again,
and Mount Sineru, wreathed in forests.

original:
Acetanāyaṁ pathavī,
aviññāya sukhaṁ dukhaṁ;
Sāpi dānabalā mayhaṁ,
sattakkhattuṁ pakampathā”ti.
text:
Even this insentient earth,
with no knowledge of happiness or sadness,
quaked seven times
at the power of my giving.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
Sasako pavanacārako;
Tiṇapaṇṇasākaphalabhakkho,
Paraheṭhanavivajjito.
text:
“Then again when I was
a hare who roamed the forest,
eating grass, leaves, vegetables, and fruit,
refraining from harming others,
title: The Wise Hare’s Conduct (Sasapaṇḍitacariya)

original:
Makkaṭo ca siṅgālo ca,
suttapoto cahaṁ tadā;
Vasāma ekasāmantā,
sāyaṁ pāto ca dissare.
text:
a monkey, a jackal,
a young otter and I
lived in the same neighborhood
and were seen together morning and evening.

original:
Ahaṁ te anusāsāmi,
kiriye kalyāṇapāpake;
‘Pāpāni parivajjetha,
kalyāṇe abhinivissatha’.
text:
I advised them
regarding good and bad deeds:
‘Shun bad deeds,
and cling to the good.’

original:
Uposathamhi divase,
candaṁ disvāna pūritaṁ;
Etesaṁ tattha ācikkhiṁ,
‘divaso ajjuposatho.
text:
Seeing the full moon
on the sabbath day,
I pointed it out to them, saying,
‘Today is the sabbath.

original:
Dānāni paṭiyādetha,
dakkhiṇeyyassa dātave;
Datvā dānaṁ dakkhiṇeyye,
upavassathuposathaṁ’.
text:
Prepare gifts
for one worthy of offerings.
Having given to one worthy of offerings,
observe the sabbath day.’

original:
Te me sādhūti vatvāna,
yathāsatti yathābalaṁ;
Dānāni paṭiyādetvā,
dakkhiṇeyyaṁ gavesisuṁ.
text:
Saying ‘good!’ to me,
they prepared gifts
according to their capacity and means,
and sought out one worthy of offerings.

original:
Ahaṁ nisajja cintesiṁ,
dānaṁ dakkhiṇanucchavaṁ;
‘Yadihaṁ labhe dakkhiṇeyyaṁ,
kiṁ me dānaṁ bhavissati.
text:
As I was sitting I thought about
what sort of gift would suit one worthy of offerings:
‘If I were to find a worthy recipient,
what gift would i give?

original:
Na me atthi tilā muggā,
māsā vā taṇḍulā ghataṁ;
Ahaṁ tiṇena yāpemi,
na sakkā tiṇa dātave.
text:
I have no sesame or mung beans,
no beans or rice or ghee.
I feed only on grass,
but that’s not something I can give.

original:
Yadi koci eti dakkhiṇeyyo,
Bhikkhāya mama santike;
Dajjāhaṁ sakamattānaṁ,
Na so tuccho gamissati’.
text:
If someone worthy of gifts comes,
seeking alms near me,
I shall give my own self:
they shall not leave empty-handed.’

original:
Mama saṅkappamaññāya,
sakko brāhmaṇavaṇṇinā;
Āsayaṁ me upāgacchi,
dānavīmaṁsanāya me.
text:
Knowing my thoughts,
Sakka in the guise of a brahmin
approached my lair
in order to test my giving.

original:
Tamahaṁ disvāna santuṭṭho,
idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ;
‘Sādhu khosi anuppatto,
ghāsahetu mamantike.
text:
Seeing him I was elated,
and said the following.
‘It is so good that you have come
to me looking for food.

original:
Adinnapubbaṁ dānavaraṁ,
ajja dassāmi te ahaṁ;
Tuvaṁ sīlaguṇūpeto,
ayuttaṁ te paraheṭhanaṁ.
text:
Today I shall give to you
a fine gift never before given.
You are furnished with virtue,
unattached to harming others.

original:
Ehi aggiṁ padīpehi,
nānākaṭṭhe samānaya;
Ahaṁ pacissamattānaṁ,
pakkaṁ tvaṁ bhakkhayissasi’.
text:
Come, light a fire,
having gathered different sticks.
I shall cook myself,
you shall eat me roasted.’

original:
‘Sādhū’ti so haṭṭhamano,
nānākaṭṭhe samānayi;
Mahantaṁ akāsi citakaṁ,
katvā aṅgāragabbhakaṁ.
text:
‘Good!’ he said happily,
and gathered different sticks.
Building a great pyre,
he placed an ember in the recess.

original:
Aggiṁ tattha padīpesi,
yathā so khippaṁ mahā bhave;
Phoṭetvā rajagate gatte,
ekamantaṁ upāvisiṁ.
text:
He lit such a fire there
that would quickly grow big.
Shaking my dusty limbs,
I withdrew to one side.

original:
Yadā mahākaṭṭhapuñjo,
āditto dhamadhamāyati;
Taduppatitvā papatiṁ,
majjhe jālasikhantare.
text:
When the great pile of sticks
was burning and blazing,
I leapt up and fell on it,
in the midst of the fiery flames.

original:
Yathā sītodakaṁ nāma,
Paviṭṭhaṁ yassa kassaci;
Sameti darathapariḷāhaṁ,
Assādaṁ deti pīti ca.
text:
Like diving
into cool water,
allaying distress and fever,
bringing satisfaction and joy.

original:
Tatheva jalitaṁ aggiṁ,
paviṭṭhassa mamaṁ tadā;
Sabbaṁ sameti darathaṁ,
yathā sītodakaṁ viya.
text:
That’s how it was
when I entered the burning flame.
It allayed distress and fever,
just like cool water.

original:
Chaviṁ cammaṁ maṁsaṁ nhāruṁ,
Aṭṭhiṁ hadayabandhanaṁ;
Kevalaṁ sakalaṁ kāyaṁ,
Brāhmaṇassa adāsahan”ti.
text:
Outer skin and inner, flesh and sinews,
bones, and heart with cords:
my whole entire body
I gave to the brahmin.”

original:
Nimi candakumāro ca,
sivi vessantaro saso;
Ahameva tadā āsiṁ,
yo te dānavare adā.

Ete dānaparikkhārā,
ete dānassa pāramī;
Jīvitaṁ yācake datvā,
imaṁ pārami pūrayiṁ.

Bhikkhāya upagataṁ disvā,
sakattānaṁ pariccajiṁ;
Dānena me samo natthi,
esā me dānapāramīti.

“Yadā ahosiṁ pavane,
kuñjaro mātuposako;
Na tadā atthi mahiyā,
guṇena mama sādiso.
text:
“Once I lived in the forest
as an elephant who provided for his mother.
At that time no one on earth
could equal my virtues.
title: The Conduct of One Who Provided for His Mother (Mātuposakacariya)

original:
Pavane disvā vanacaro,
rañño maṁ paṭivedayi;
‘Tavānucchavo mahārāja,
gajo vasati kānane.
text:
Seeing me in the forest, a forester
informed the king about me.
‘Great King, an elephant that befits you
is dwelling in the forest grove.

original:
Na tassa parikkhāyattho,
napi āḷakakāsuyā;
Saha gahite soṇḍāya,
sayameva idhehi’ti.
text:
No need to dig a moat around him,
nor tether him to a post in a pit.
Taken by the trunk,
he will come here by himself.’

original:
Tassa taṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
rājāpi tuṭṭhamānaso;
Pesesi hatthidamakaṁ,
chekācariyaṁ susikkhitaṁ.
text:
When he heard these words,
the king, elated,
sent an elephant-tamer,
a well-trained and expert tutor.

original:
Gantvā so hatthidamako,
addasa padumassare;
Bhisamuḷālaṁ uddharantaṁ,
yāpanatthāya mātuyā.
text:
When the elephant-tamer reached there,
he saw me in a lotus pond,
pulling out lotus roots
to feed my mother.

original:
Viññāya me sīlaguṇaṁ,
lakkhaṇaṁ upadhārayi;
‘Ehi puttā’ti vatvāna,
mama soṇḍāya aggahi.
text:
Discerning my moral virtue,
he checked me for marks.
Saying, ‘Come, child’,
he took me by the trunk.

original:
Yaṁ me tadā pākatikaṁ,
sarīrānugataṁ balaṁ;
Ajja nāgasahassānaṁ,
balena samasādisaṁ.
text:
What was at that time
the natural strength of my body,
would equal a thousand
of the elephants of today.

original:
Yadihaṁ tesaṁ pakuppeyyaṁ,
upetānaṁ gahaṇāya maṁ;
Paṭibalo bhave tesaṁ,
yāva rajjampi mānusaṁ.
text:
If I had been upset
with those who came to capture me,
I would have had the power
to defeat even a kingdom of men.

original:
Api cāhaṁ sīlarakkhāya,
Sīlapāramipūriyā;
Na karomi citte aññathattaṁ,
Pakkhipantaṁ mamāḷake.
text:
Nevertheless, for the sake of guarding my ethics,
and fulfilling my perfection of ethics,
I did not let my mind change,
even as they caged me.

original:
Yadi te maṁ tattha koṭṭeyyuṁ,
pharasūhi tomarehi ca;
Neva tesaṁ pakuppeyyaṁ,
sīlakhaṇḍabhayā mamā”ti.
text:
And even were they to beat me
with hatchets and lances,
I would never become upset,
for fear of violating my ethics.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
bhūridatto mahiddhiko;
Virūpakkhena mahāraññā,
devalokamagañchahaṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
Bhūridatta, a dragon of great psychic power,
together with Virūpakkha the Great King
I went to a heavenly realm.
title: The Dragon Bhūridatta’s Conduct (Bhūridattacariya)

original:
Tattha passitvāhaṁ deve,
ekantaṁ sukhasamappite;
Taṁ saggagamanatthāya,
sīlabbataṁ samādiyiṁ.
text:
There I saw gods
wholly given over to pleasure.
For the sake of going to that heaven,
I undertook the observance of ethics.

original:
Sarīrakiccaṁ katvāna,
bhutvā yāpanamattakaṁ;
Caturo aṅge adhiṭṭhāya,
semi vammikamuddhani.
text:
After tending to my physical needs,
and eating enough to get by,
I resolved on the four factors,
and lay down atop a termite mound, thinking:

original:
‘Chaviyā cammena maṁsena,
Nahāruaṭṭhikehi vā;
Yassa etena karaṇīyaṁ,
Dinnaṁyeva harātu so’.
text:
‘My outer skin and inner, flesh,
sinews and bones:
whoever has use for these,
they are already given, please take them.’

original:
Saṁsito akataññunā,
ālampāyano mamaggahi;
Peḷāya pakkhipitvāna,
kīḷeti maṁ tahiṁ tahiṁ.
text:
While lying there the ingrate
Ālampāyana grabbed me.
He threw me in a basket
and made me perform in places all over.

original:
Peḷāya pakkhipantepi,
sammaddantepi pāṇinā;
Ālampāyane na kuppāmi,
sīlakhaṇḍabhayā mama.
text:
Though thrown in a basket
and crushed by his hands,
I did not get upset with Ālampāyana,
for fear of breaking my ethics.

original:
Sakajīvitapariccāgo,
tiṇato lahuko mama;
Sīlavītikkamo mayhaṁ,
pathavīuppatanaṁ viya.
text:
To give up my own life
was as light as a blade of grass.
To transgress my ethical principles
was like overturning the earth.

original:
Nirantaraṁ jātisataṁ,
cajeyyaṁ mama jīvitaṁ;
Neva sīlaṁ pabhindeyyaṁ,
catuddīpāna hetupi.
text:
In a hundred successive lives
I would give up my own life.
I would not even violate my ethics
for the sake of the four continents.

original:
Api cāhaṁ sīlarakkhāya,
Sīlapāramipūriyā;
Na karomi citte aññathattaṁ,
Pakkhipantampi peḷake”ti.
text:
For the sake of protecting ethics,
and fulfilling my perfection of ethics,
I did not let my mind change,
even when thrown in a basket.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
campeyyako mahiddhiko;
Tadāpi dhammiko āsiṁ,
sīlabbatasamappito.
text:
“Then again when I was
Campeyyaka, a dragon of great psychic power,
I was just,
furnished with precepts and vows.
title: The Dragon Campeyyaka’s Conduct (Campeyyanāgacariya)

original:
Tadāpi maṁ dhammacāriṁ,
upavutthaṁ uposathaṁ;
Ahituṇḍiko gahetvāna,
rājadvāramhi kīḷati.
text:
Then the snake-charmer who caught me
lived righteously,
observing the Sabbath,
and he made me perform at the royal gate.

original:
Yaṁ yaṁ so vaṇṇaṁ cintayi,
nīlaṁva pītalohitaṁ;
Tassa cittānuvattanto,
homi cintitasannibho.
text:
Whatever color he thought of—
blue, yellow, or red—
I conformed to his wish,
taking the appearance of his thought.

original:
Thalaṁ kareyyamudakaṁ,
udakampi thalaṁ kare;
Yadihaṁ tassa pakuppeyyaṁ,
khaṇena chārikaṁ kare.
text:
I could turn dry land to water,
and water to dry land.
If I were upset with him
I could reduce him to ash in an instant.

original:
Yadi cittavasī hessaṁ,
parihāyissāmi sīlato;
Sīlena parihīnassa,
uttamattho na sijjhati.
text:
If I was under the sway of my thoughts,
I would have fallen from my ethics.
But one who has fallen from their ethics
does not succeed at the highest goal.

original:
Kāmaṁ bhijjatuyaṁ kāyo,
idheva vikirīyatu;
Neva sīlaṁ pabhindeyyaṁ,
vikirante bhusaṁ viyā”ti.
text:
Gladly, let this body be broken!
Let it be scattered in this very place!
Not even for that would I break my ethics,
if it were being scattered like hay.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
cūḷabodhi susīlavā;
Bhavaṁ disvāna bhayato,
nekkhammaṁ abhinikkhamiṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
the very virtuous Cūḷabodhi,
seeing rebirth as fearful,
I renounced worldly life.
title: Cūḷabodhi’s Conduct (Cūḷabodhicariya)

original:
Yā me dutiyikā āsi,
brāhmaṇī kanakasannibhā;
Sāpi vaṭṭe anapekkhā,
nekkhammaṁ abhinikkhami.
text:
She who had been my partner,
a brahmin lady with golden skin,
unconcerned with the cycle of rebirths,
also renounced worldly life.

original:
Nirālayā chinnabandhū,
anapekkhā kule gaṇe;
Carantā gāmanigamaṁ,
bārāṇasimupāgamuṁ.
text:
Without clinging, cutting off family,
unconcerned with family or group,
we walked from village to town
until we reached Varanasi.

original:
Tattha vasāma nipakā,
asaṁsaṭṭhā kule gaṇe;
Nirākule appasadde,
rājuyyāne vasāmubho.
text:
There we lived alert,
mixing not with a family or group.
Quiet and undisturbed,
we both stayed in the royal park.

original:
Uyyānadassanaṁ gantvā,
rājā addasa brāhmaṇiṁ;
Upagamma mamaṁ pucchi,
‘tuyhesā kā kassa bhariyā’.
text:
Visiting the park,
the king saw the brahmin lady.
He approached me and asked,
‘Is she your wife? Or whose is she?’

original:
Evaṁ vutte, ahaṁ tassa,
idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ;
‘Na mayhaṁ bhariyā esā,
sahadhammā ekasāsanī’.
text:
When he said this, to him
I said the following.
‘She is not my wife.
We share the same teaching and belief.’

original:
Tissā sārattagadhito,
gāhāpetvāna ceṭake;
Nippīḷayanto balasā,
antepuraṁ pavesayi.
text:
Infatuated with her,
he had his men seize her.
Compelling her by force
he brought her to the royal compound.

original:
Odapattakiyā mayhaṁ,
sahajā ekasāsanī;
Ākaḍḍhitvā nayantiyā,
kopo me upapajjatha.
text:
She who became mine by touching a water-jar,
born together, one in beliefs,
when he dragged her away,
I felt so angry.

original:
Saha kope samuppanne,
sīlabbatamanussariṁ;
Tattheva kopaṁ niggaṇhiṁ,
nādāsiṁ vaḍḍhitūpari.
text:
Together with the arising of anger,
I remembered my precepts and vows,
and right there controlled my anger,
I did not allow it to grow.

original:
Yadi naṁ brāhmaṇiṁ koci,
koṭṭeyya tiṇhasattiyā;
Neva sīlaṁ pabhindeyyaṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā.
text:
If anyone were to attack
that brahmin lady with a sharp knife,
not even for that would I violate my ethics,
because it was solely for awakening.

original:
Na mesā brāhmaṇī dessā,
napi me balaṁ na vijjati;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā sīlānurakkhisan”ti.
text:
I did not dislike the brahmin lady,
nor did I lack the strength.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
that’s why I guarded my ethics.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
mahiṁso pavanacārako;
Pavaḍḍhakāyo balavā,
mahanto bhīmadassano.
text:
“Then again when I was
a buffalo who roamed the forest,
large in body and strong,
big and scary to see.
title: The Buffalo King’s Conduct (Mahiṁsarājacariya)

original:
Pabbhāre giridugge ca,
rukkhamūle dakāsaye;
Hotettha ṭhānaṁ mahiṁsānaṁ,
koci koci tahiṁ tahiṁ.
text:
In a cave, a craggy hillside,
at a tree root or a waterhole,
there’d be somewhere for buffalos,
in one place or another.

original:
Vicaranto brahāraññe,
ṭhānaṁ addasa bhaddakaṁ;
Taṁ ṭhānaṁ upagantvāna,
tiṭṭhāmi ca sayāmi ca.
text:
Wandering the mighty forest,
I saw a fine spot.
Having gone there,
I stood and lay to rest.

original:
Athettha kapimāgantvā,
pāpo anariyo lahu;
Khandhe nalāṭe bhamuke,
mutteti ohadeti taṁ.
text:
Then a monkey came along,
wicked, ignoble, and nimble.
On my shoulder, forehead, and eyebrows,
he peed and pooed.

original:
Sakimpi divasaṁ dutiyaṁ,
tatiyaṁ catutthampi ca;
Dūseti maṁ sabbakālaṁ,
tena homi upadduto.
text:
Not just that day, but a second,
a third, and a fourth;
he soiled me all the time,
he was harrying me.

original:
Mamaṁ upaddutaṁ disvā,
yakkho maṁ idamabravi;
‘Nāsehetaṁ chavaṁ pāpaṁ,
siṅgehi ca khurehi ca’.
text:
Seeing me being harried,
a spirit said to me:
‘Kill that vile, wicked thing
with your horns and hooves.’

original:
Evaṁ vutte, tadā yakkhe,
ahaṁ taṁ idamabraviṁ;
‘Kiṁ tvaṁ makkhesi kuṇapena,
pāpena anariyena maṁ.
text:
When he spoke, I said
this to that spirit:
‘Why would you smear me
with a wicked, ignoble carcass?

original:
Yadihaṁ tassa pakuppeyyaṁ,
tato hīnataro bhave;
Sīlañca me pabhijjeyya,
viññū ca garaheyyu maṁ.
text:
If I were upset with him
I would degrade myself,
violating my ethics,
and being criticized by sensible people.

original:
Hīḷitā jīvitā vāpi,
parisuddhena mataṁ varaṁ;
Kyāhaṁ jīvitahetūpi,
kāhāmi paraheṭhanaṁ’.
text:
Better to die from purity
than live in shame.
How could I, for the sake of life,
harm another?’

original:
Mamevāyaṁ maññamāno,
aññepevaṁ karissati;
Teva tassa vadhissanti,
sā me mutti bhavissati.
text:
Thinking of me, this one
will do the same to others,
and for that they will kill him.
Then I shall be free.

original:
Hīnamajjhimaukkaṭṭhe,
sahanto avamānitaṁ;
Evaṁ labhati sappañño,
manasā yathāpatthitan”ti.
text:
Forgiving disrespect
from the low, middle and high,
the wise one gains
their heart’s desire.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
sutattakanakasannibho;
Migarājā ruru nāma,
paramasīlasamāhito.
text:
“Then again when I was
the king of deer named Ruru,
in appearance I was like burnished gold,
focused on the highest ethics.
title: Ruru the Deer King’s Conduct (Rurumigarājacariya)

original:
Ramme padese ramaṇīye,
vivitte amanussake;
Tattha vāsaṁ upagañchiṁ,
gaṅgākūle manorame.
text:
There was a pleasant, delightful region,
free of humans,
so I went there and stayed
on a lovely bank of the Ganges.

original:
Atha upari gaṅgāya,
dhanikehi paripīḷito;
Puriso gaṅgāya papati,
‘jīvāmi vā marāmi vā’.
text:
Then a man upstream,
harassed by creditors,
fell into the Ganges, thinking,
‘I live or I die!’

original:
Rattindivaṁ so gaṅgāya,
vuyhamāno mahodake;
Ravanto karuṇaṁ ravaṁ,
majjhe gaṅgāya gacchati.
text:
Day and night in the Ganges
he was swept along the stream,
crying out pitifully,
along the middle of the Ganges.

original:
Tassāhaṁ saddaṁ sutvāna,
karuṇaṁ paridevato;
Gaṅgāya tīre ṭhatvāna,
apucchiṁ ‘kosi tvaṁ naro’.
text:
When I heard the sound
of his pitiful crying,
I stood on the Ganges bank
and asked, ‘What man are you?’

original:
So me puṭṭho ca byākāsi,
attano karaṇaṁ tadā;
‘Dhanikehi bhīto tasito,
pakkhandohaṁ mahānadiṁ’.
text:
When asked he explained
to me his own deed:
‘I was so scared of my creditors,
I jumped in the great river!’

original:
Tassa katvāna kāruññaṁ,
cajitvā mama jīvitaṁ;
Pavisitvā nīhariṁ tassa,
andhakāramhi rattiyā.
text:
Taking pity on him,
surrendering my own life,
I entered and dragged him out
in the darkness of the night.

original:
Assatthakālamaññāya,
tassāhaṁ idamabraviṁ;
‘Ekaṁ taṁ varaṁ yācāmi,
mā maṁ kassaci pāvada’.
text:
When I knew he had recovered,
I said to him,
‘I ask of you one favor:
tell no one about me.’

original:
Nagaraṁ gantvāna ācikkhi,
pucchito dhanahetuko;
Rājānaṁ so gahetvāna,
upagañchi mamantikaṁ.
text:
But once he had returned to the city,
for the sake of money he told when asked.
Taking the king,
he drew close to me.

All that I had done
was related to the king.
When the king heard this,
he fitted his arrow, thinking,
‘Right here I shall kill
this ignoble betrayer of a friend.’

original:
Tamahaṁ anurakkhanto,
nimminiṁ mama attanā;
‘Tiṭṭhateso mahārāja,
kāmakāro bhavāmi te’.
text:
I protected him,
substituting myself:
‘Let him be, Great King.
I shall carry out your pleasure.’

original:
Anurakkhiṁ mama sīlaṁ,
nārakkhiṁ mama jīvitaṁ;
Sīlavā hi tadā āsiṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā”ti.
text:
I guarded my ethics,
not my life.
For then I was ethical,
because it was solely for awakening.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
jaṭilo uggatāpano;
Mātaṅgo nāma nāmena,
sīlavā susamāhito.
text:
“Then again when I was
a matted-hair ascetic of severe penance,
Mātaṅga was my name,
I was virtuous and serene.
title: Mātaṅga’s Conduct (Mātaṅgacariya)

original:
Ahañca brāhmaṇo eko,
gaṅgākūle vasāmubho;
Ahaṁ vasāmi upari,
heṭṭhā vasati brāhmaṇo.
text:
A brahmin and I both lived
on a bank of the Ganges.
I stayed upstream,
the brahmin downstream.

original:
Vicaranto anukūlamhi,
uddhaṁ me assamaddasa;
Tattha maṁ paribhāsetvā,
abhisapi muddhaphālanaṁ.
text:
Wandering along the riverbank,
he saw my hermitage upstream.
Then he abused and cursed me,
that my head would split in seven.

original:
Yadihaṁ tassa pakuppeyyaṁ,
yadi sīlaṁ na gopaye;
Oloketvānahaṁ tassa,
kareyyaṁ chārikaṁ viya.
text:
If I were upset with him
and if I were not taking care of my ethics,
then just with a glance
I could have reduced him to ashes.

original:
Yaṁ so tadā maṁ abhisapi,
kupito duṭṭhamānaso;
Tasseva matthake nipati,
yogena taṁ pamocayiṁ.
text:
But when he cursed me then,
so angry and bitter-hearted,
it fell right back on his own head:
I freed him from that yoke.

original:
Anurakkhiṁ mama sīlaṁ,
nārakkhiṁ mama jīvitaṁ;
Sīlavā hi tadā āsiṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā”ti.
text:
I guarded my ethics,
not my life.
For then I was ethical,
because it was solely for awakening.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
mahāpakkho mahiddhiko;
Dhammo nāma mahāyakkho,
sabbalokānukampako.
text:
“Then again when I was
of great retinue and psychic power,
a great spirit named Dhamma,
I had sympathy for the whole world.
title: The Deity Dhamma’s Conduct (Dhammadevaputtacariya)

original:
Dasakusalakammapathe,
samādapento mahājanaṁ;
Carāmi gāmanigamaṁ,
samitto saparijjano.
text:
Establishing the populace
in the ten ways of skillful deeds,
I wandered from village to town,
with friends and associates.

original:
Pāpo kadariyo yakkho,
dīpento dasa pāpake;
Sopettha mahiyā carati,
samitto saparijjano.
text:
A wicked, miserly spirit
promoting the ten wicked ways
was also wandering the earth
with friends and associates.

original:
Dhammavādī adhammo ca,
ubho paccanikā mayaṁ;
Dhure dhuraṁ ghaṭṭayantā,
samimhā paṭipathe ubho.
text:
The righteous and unrighteous,
we were each other’s foe.
Slamming chariot poles,
we collided together.

original:
Kalaho vattatī bhesmā,
kalyāṇapāpakassa ca;
Maggā okkamanatthāya,
mahāyuddho upaṭṭhito.
text:
A dreadful quarrel ensued
between the good and the ill,
a great war loomed
aiming to push the other off the road.

original:
Yadihaṁ tassa kuppeyyaṁ,
yadi bhinde tapoguṇaṁ;
Sahaparijanaṁ tassa,
rajabhūtaṁ kareyyahaṁ.
text:
If I had been upset with him,
if I had broken my asceticism,
I could have reduced him to dust,
together with his companions.

original:
Api cāhaṁ sīlarakkhāya,
nibbāpetvāna mānasaṁ;
Saha janenokkamitvā,
pathaṁ pāpassa dāsahaṁ.
text:
Nevertheless, for the sake of guarding my ethics,
I quelled my heart.
I left the road with my folk,
giving it to the wicked one.

original:
Saha pathato okkante,
katvā cittassa nibbutiṁ;
Vivaraṁ adāsi pathavī,
pāpayakkhassa tāvade”ti.
text:
As soon as I stepped down off the path,
and I had quelled my mind,
the earth opened up
for that wicked spirit.”

original:
“Pañcālaraṭṭhe nagaravare,
Kapilāyaṁ puruttame;
Rājā jayaddiso nāma,
Sīlaguṇamupāgato.
text:
“In the kingdom of Pañcāla, in the eminent city,
the capital named Kapilā,
the king named Jayaddisa
was furnished with virtuous qualities.
title: Alīnasattu’s Conduct (Alīnasattucariya)

original:
Tassa rañño ahaṁ putto,
Sutadhammo susīlavā;
Alīnasatto guṇavā,
Anurakkhaparijano sadā.
text:
I was that king’s son,
well educated and virtuous;
Alīnasattu of fine qualities,
I always cared for the attendants.

original:
Pitā me migavaṁ gantvā,
porisādaṁ upāgami;
So me pitumaggahesi,
‘bhakkhosi mama mā cali’.
text:
My father had gone deer hunting
when he came across a cannibal,
who seized my father, saying,
‘You are my prey, don’t move!’

original:
Tassa taṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
bhīto tasitavedhito;
Ūrukkhambho ahu tassa,
disvāna porisādakaṁ.
text:
When he heard these words,
he was scared and trembled with fear,
his thighs became stiff
when he saw the cannibal.

original:
Migavaṁ gahetvā muñcassu,
katvā āgamanaṁ puna;
Brāhmaṇassa dhanaṁ datvā,
pitā āmantayī mamaṁ.
text:
‘Let me go, take the deer meat!’ he said,
‘I promise to return.’
Having paid the brahmin,
my father said to me:

original:
‘Rajjaṁ putta paṭipajja,
mā pamajji puraṁ idaṁ;
Kataṁ me porisādena,
mama āgamanaṁ puna’.
text:
‘Son, rule the realm.
Do not neglect this city.
I promised the cannibal
that I will return.’

original:
Mātāpitū ca vanditvā,
nimminitvāna attanā;
Nikkhipitvā dhanuṁ khaggaṁ,
porisādaṁ upāgamiṁ.
text:
I bowed to my mother and father,
and substituted myself.
Tossing my bow and sword,
I approached the cannibal.

original:
Sasatthahatthūpagataṁ,
kadāci so tasissati;
Tena bhijjissati sīlaṁ,
parittāsaṁ kate mayi.
text:
Perhaps if I have weapons in hand
that might make him afraid.
And that would violate my ethics,
were I to frighten him.

original:
Sīlakhaṇḍabhayā mayhaṁ,
tassa dessaṁ na byāhariṁ;
Mettacitto hitavādī,
idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ.
text:
For fear of violating my ethics,
I said nothing hateful to him.
Lovingly and beneficially,
I said the following.

original:
‘Ujjālehi mahāaggiṁ,
papatissāmi rukkhato;
Tvaṁ pakkakālamaññāya,
bhakkhaya maṁ pitāmaha’.
text:
‘Kindle a great fire.
I will drop into it from a tree.
When you know I am cooked,
eat me, Grandfather.’

original:
Iti sīlavataṁ hetu,
nārakkhiṁ mama jīvitaṁ;
Pabbājesiṁ cahaṁ tassa,
sadā pāṇātipātikan”ti.
text:
And so for the sake of my ethical vows
I did not protect my life.
And I drove out forever
his attacks on living creatures.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
saṅkhapālo mahiddhiko;
Dāṭhāvudho ghoraviso,
dvijivho uragādhibhū.
text:
“Then again when I was
Saṅkhapāla, a dragon of great psychic power,
deadly-fanged, lethally venomous,
two-tongued, lord of serpents.
title: Saṅkhapāla’s Conduct (Saṅkhapālacariya)

original:
Catuppathe mahāmagge,
nānājanasamākule;
Caturo aṅge adhiṭṭhāya,
tattha vāsamakappayiṁ.
text:
At a crossroad on a highway
crowded with many people,
I resolved on the four factors,
and made my home there.

original:
Chaviyā cammena maṁsena,
Nahāruaṭṭhikehi vā;
Yassa etena karaṇīyaṁ,
Dinnaṁyeva harātu so.
text:
‘My outer skin and inner, flesh,
sinews and bones:
whoever has use for these,
they are already given, please take them.’

original:
Addasaṁsu bhojaputtā,
kharā luddā akāruṇā;
Upagañchuṁ mamaṁ tattha,
daṇḍamuggarapāṇino.
text:
Seeing me, the Bhojans,
those violent and pitiless hunters,
came to me there
with sticks and hammers in their hands.

original:
Nāsāya vinivijjhitvā,
naṅguṭṭhe piṭṭhikaṇṭake;
Kāje āropayitvāna,
bhojaputtā hariṁsu maṁ.
text:
Having pierced my nose,
tail, and spine,
and fastened me to a pole,
the Bhojans carried me away.

original:
Sasāgarantaṁ pathaviṁ,
sakānanaṁ sapabbataṁ;
Icchamāno cahaṁ tattha,
nāsāvātena jhāpaye.
text:
The earth from sea to sea,
with its forests and mountains—
had I wished, right there
I could have burnt it up with a blast from my nose.

original:
Sūlehi vinivijjhante,
Koṭṭayantepi sattibhi;
Bhojaputte na kuppāmi,
Esā me sīlapāramī”ti.
text:
Though pierced with stakes,
and stabbed with knives,
I did not get upset with the Bhojans:
this is my perfection of ethics.”

original:
Ete nava sīlabalā,
parikkhārā padesikā;
Jīvitaṁ parirakkhitvā,
sīlāni anurakkhisaṁ.

Saṅkhapālassa me sato,
sabbakālampi jīvitaṁ;
Yassa kassaci niyyattaṁ,
tasmā sā sīlapāramīti.

“Yadāhaṁ amitayaso,
Rājaputto yudhañjayo;
Ussāvabinduṁ sūriyātape,
Patitaṁ disvāna saṁvijiṁ.
text:
“When I was Prince Yudhañjaya
of infinite fame,
I was stirred with urgency on seeing
a fallen dewdrop in the heat of the sun.
title: Yudhañjaya’s Conduct (Yudhañjayacariya)

original:
Taññevādhipatiṁ katvā,
saṁvegamanubrūhayiṁ;
Mātāpitū ca vanditvā,
pabbajjamanuyācahaṁ.
text:
Taking that to be of prime importance,
I fostered that urgency.
I bowed to my mother and father,
and begged permission to go forth.

original:
Yācanti maṁ pañjalikā,
sanegamā saraṭṭhakā;
‘Ajjeva putta paṭipajja,
iddhaṁ phītaṁ mahāmahiṁ’.
text:
With cupped palms,
along with the citizens of town and country, they asked,
‘This very day, rule this great land,
so successful and prosperous.’

original:
Sarājake sahorodhe,
sanegame saraṭṭhake;
Karuṇaṁ paridevante,
anapekkhova pariccajiṁ.
text:
The King and the Queens,
with the citizens of town and country,
cried pitifully,
as I forsook unconcerned.

original:
Kevalaṁ pathaviṁ rajjaṁ,
ñātiparijanaṁ yasaṁ;
Cajamāno na cintesiṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā.
text:
Kingship over the entire earth,
family, retinue, and fame—
I gave them up without a second thought,
because it was solely for awakening.

original:
Mātāpitā na me dessā,
napi me dessaṁ mahāyasaṁ;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā rajjaṁ pariccajin”ti.
text:
I had no dislike of my parents,
nor did I dislike the great fame.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I forsook kingship.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
indapatthe puruttame;
Kāmito dayito putto,
somanassoti vissuto.
text:
“Then again when I was
in Indapatta, the capital city,
I was a loved and cherished child
renowned as Somanassa.
title: Somanassa’s Conduct (Somanassacariya)

original:
Sīlavā guṇasampanno,
kalyāṇapaṭibhānavā;
Vuḍḍhāpacāyī hirīmā,
saṅgahesu ca kovido.
text:
I was ethical, full of good qualities,
of fine and eloquent speech,
honoring elders, conscientious,
and expert in the methods of inclusiveness.

original:
Tassa rañño patikaro,
ahosi kuhakatāpaso;
Ārāmaṁ mālāvacchañca,
ropayitvāna jīvati.
text:
Now there was this charlatan renunciant
who was favored by the king.
He made a living by cultivating
an orchard and flowering shrubs.

original:
Tamahaṁ disvāna kuhakaṁ,
thusarāsiṁva ataṇḍulaṁ;
Dumaṁva anto susiraṁ,
kadaliṁva asārakaṁ.
text:
Seeing he was a charlatan,
like a pile of chaff without grain,
like a hollow tree,
like a plantain tree with no core, I thought:

original:
Natthimassa sataṁ dhammo,
sāmaññāpagato ayaṁ;
Hirīsukkadhammajahito,
jīvitavuttikāraṇā.
text:
‘There is no good in him,
he has strayed from asceticism.
He has left the bright qualities of conscience
for the sake of making a living.’

original:
Kupito ahu paccanto,
aṭavīhi parantihi;
Taṁ nisedhetuṁ gacchanto,
anusāsi pitā mamaṁ.
text:
Then the borders were in turmoil
by wild frontier savages.
Before going to put an end to it,
my father instructed me:

original:
‘Mā pamajji tuvaṁ tāta,
jaṭilaṁ uggatāpanaṁ;
Yadicchakaṁ pavattehi,
sabbakāmadado hi so’.
text:
‘My dear, do not neglect
the matted-hair ascetic of severe penance.
He is the granter of our wishes,
give him all he desires.’

original:
Tamahaṁ gantvānupaṭṭhānaṁ,
Idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ;
‘Kacci te gahapati kusalaṁ,
Kiṁ vā te āharīyatu’.
text:
I went then to serve him,
and said the following.
‘I hope you are well, householder.
Is there anything I can bring for you?’

original:
Tena so kupito āsi,
kuhako mānanissito;
‘Ghātāpemi tuvaṁ ajja,
raṭṭhā pabbājayāmi vā’.
text:
At that he was upset with me,
that prideful charlatan.
‘I’ll have you killed right now!
Or banished from the realm!’

original:
Nisedhayitvā paccantaṁ,
rājā kuhakamabravi;
‘Kacci te bhante khamanīyaṁ,
sammāno te pavattito’.
text:
After putting an end to the border conflict,
the king said to the charlatan,
‘I hope you’re keeping well, sir,
and honors were served you?’

original:
Tassa ācikkhatī pāpo,
kumāro yathā nāsiyo;
Tassa taṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
āṇāpesi mahīpati.
text:
That wicked one told him
how the prince deserved execution.
When he heard these words,
the Lord of the Earth commanded:

original:
‘Sīsaṁ tattheva chinditvā,
katvāna catukhaṇḍikaṁ;
Rathiyā rathiyaṁ dassetha,
sā gati jaṭilahīḷitā’.
text:
‘Cut off his head right there!
Saw his corpse into four pieces!
And then show them from street to street:
this is the fate of one who shames the ascetic.’

original:
Tattha kāraṇikā gantvā,
caṇḍā luddā akāruṇā;
Mātu aṅke nisinnassa,
ākaḍḍhitvā nayanti maṁ.
text:
Right away left the punishers—
fierce, violent and pitiless.
They dragged me from my mother’s lap
and led me away.

original:
Tesāhaṁ evamavacaṁ,
bandhataṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ;
‘Rañño dassetha maṁ khippaṁ,
rājakiriyāni atthi me’.
text:
I said to them
as they bound me with tight bonds:
‘Present me to the king right now,
I have an issue for the king!’

original:
Te maṁ rañño dassayiṁsu,
pāpassa pāpasevino;
Disvāna taṁ saññāpesiṁ,
mamañca vasamānayiṁ.
text:
They presented me to the king,
follower of the wicked one and his wicked ways.
On seeing me, I persuaded him
and brought him under my influence.

original:
So maṁ tattha khamāpesi,
mahārajjamadāsi me;
Sohaṁ tamaṁ dālayitvā,
pabbajiṁ anagāriyaṁ.
text:
He asked for my forgiveness then,
and offered me the kingdom.
But having burst the darkness asunder,
I went forth to homelessness.

original:
Na me dessaṁ mahārajjaṁ,
kāmabhogo na dessiyo;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā rajjaṁ pariccajin”ti.
text:
I did not dislike great kingship,
nor did I dislike sensual enjoyment.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I forsook kingship.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
kāsirājassa atrajo;
Ayogharamhi saṁvaḍḍho,
nāmenāsi ayogharo.
text:
“Then again when I was
the true-born son of the king of Kāsi,
I grew up in an iron house,
so I was named Ayoghara.
title: Ayoghara’s Conduct (Ayogharacariya)

original:
‘Dukkhena jīvito laddho,
saṁpīḷe patiposito;
Ajjeva putta paṭipajja,
kevalaṁ vasudhaṁ imaṁ’.
text:
‘Your life has been a painful one,
as you’ve been raised in confinement.
Today, my son, rule
the entirety of this land.’

original:
Saraṭṭhakaṁ sanigamaṁ,
sajanaṁ vanditva khattiyaṁ;
Añjaliṁ paggahetvāna,
idaṁ vacanamabraviṁ.
text:
Having bowed to the citizens of country and town,
the king and his people,
I raised my cupped palms
and said the following.

original:
‘Ye keci mahiyā sattā,
hīnamukkaṭṭhamajjhimā;
Nirārakkhā sake gehe,
vaḍḍhanti sakañātibhi.
text:
‘All the creatures of this earth—
low, middle, or high—
are unprotected in their own home,
in which they grew up with their families.

original:
Idaṁ loke uttariyaṁ,
saṁpīḷe mama posanaṁ;
Ayogharamhi saṁvaḍḍho,
appabhe candasūriye.
text:
It was unique in the world
to be raised in confinement.
I grew up in an iron house,
scarcely lit by sun or moon.

original:
Pūtikuṇapasampuṇṇā,
muccitvā mātukucchito;
Tato ghoratare dukkhe,
puna pakkhittayoghare.
text:
Filled with rotting carcass,
I escaped my mother’s womb.
Then to a viler suffering
I was tossed in an iron house.

original:
Yadihaṁ tādisaṁ patvā,
dukkhaṁ paramadāruṇaṁ;
Rajjesu yadi rajjāmi,
pāpānaṁ uttamo siyaṁ.
text:
Having fallen into such
appallingly dreadful suffering,
if I desired kingships,
I’d be the worst of the worst.

original:
Ukkaṇṭhitomhi kāyena,
rajjenamhi anatthiko;
Nibbutiṁ pariyesissaṁ,
yattha maṁ maccu na maddiye’.
text:
I’m fed up with the body,
I have no need for kingship.
I shall seek quenching
where Death will not crush me.’

original:
Evāhaṁ cintayitvāna,
viravante mahājane;
Nāgova bandhanaṁ chetvā,
pāvisiṁ kānanaṁ vanaṁ.
text:
Reflecting in this way,
as the great crowd wailed,
like a bull elephant bursting his ropes,
I entered the forest grove.

original:
Mātāpitā na me dessā,
napi me dessaṁ mahāyasaṁ;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā rajjaṁ pariccajin”ti.
text:
I had no dislike of my parents,
nor did I dislike the great fame.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I forsook kingship.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
kāsīnaṁ puravaruttame;
Bhaginī ca bhātaro satta,
nibbattā sotthiye kule.
text:
“Then again when I was
in the capital citadel of Kāsi,
a sister and seven brothers
were born in a learned family.
title: The Conduct of the Lotus-eaters (Bhisacariya)

original:
Etesaṁ pubbajo āsiṁ,
hirīsukkamupāgato;
Bhavaṁ disvāna bhayato,
nekkhammābhirato ahaṁ.
text:
I was the first-born of them all,
furnishing with pure conscience.
Seeing rebirth as fearful,
I longed for renunciation.

original:
Mātāpitūhi pahitā,
sahāyā ekamānasā;
Kāmehi maṁ nimantenti,
‘kulavaṁsaṁ dharehi’ti.
text:
Sent for by my mother and father,
my friends with one mind
invited me to enjoy sensual pleasures, saying:
‘Maintain the family lineage.’

original:
Yaṁ tesaṁ vacanaṁ vuttaṁ,
gihīdhamme sukhāvahaṁ;
Taṁ me ahosi kaṭhinaṁ,
tattaphālasamaṁ viya.
text:
The words they said
about the ways a householder can find happiness,
were hard for me to hear,
like a heated ploughshare.

original:
Te maṁ tadā ukkhipantaṁ,
pucchiṁsu patthitaṁ mama;
‘Kiṁ tvaṁ patthayase samma,
yadi kāme na bhuñjasi’.
text:
When I turned down their proposal,
they asked me what I wished for:
‘My dear, what is it that you wish,
since you do not long for sensual pleasures?’

original:
Tesāhaṁ evamavacaṁ,
atthakāmo hitesinaṁ;
‘Nāhaṁ patthemi gihībhāvaṁ,
nekkhammābhirato ahaṁ’.
text:
I spoke to my beneficiaries,
wanting what is best.
‘I wish not for the householder’s state,
I long for renunciation.’

original:
Te mayhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
pitu mātu ca sāvayuṁ;
Mātāpitā evamāhu,
‘sabbeva pabbajāma bho’.
text:
Hearing my words,
they told my mother and father.
My parents said this:
‘Sirs, let all of us go forth!’

original:
Ubho mātāpitā mayhaṁ,
bhaginī ca satta bhātaro;
Amitadhanaṁ chaḍḍayitvā,
pāvisimhā mahāvanan”ti.
text:
So both my mother and father,
sister and seven brothers,
discarding countless riches,
entered the great forest.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
nagare brahmavaḍḍhane;
Tattha kulavare seṭṭhe,
mahāsāle ajāyahaṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
in the city of Brahmavaḍḍhana,
I was reborn there
in a fine, wealthy, and eminent family.
title: Soṇa the Astute’s Conduct (Soṇapaṇḍitacariya)

original:
Tadāpi lokaṁ disvāna,
Andhībhūtaṁ tamotthaṭaṁ;
Cittaṁ bhavato patikuṭati,
Tuttavegahataṁ viya.
text:
Even so, I saw that the world
had become blind, smothered in darkness.
My mind recoiled from rebirth,
as if harshly pricked by a goad.

original:
Disvāna vividhaṁ pāpaṁ,
evaṁ cintesahaṁ tadā;
‘Kadāhaṁ gehā nikkhamma,
pavisissāmi kānanaṁ’.
text:
Seeing the many forms of wickedness,
I thought to myself:
‘When shall I leave the house
and enter the forest?’

original:
Tadāpi maṁ nimantesuṁ,
kāmabhogehi ñātayo;
Tesampi chandamācikkhiṁ,
‘mā nimantetha tehi maṁ’.
text:
Then too my relatives invited me
to enjoy the pleasures of the senses.
I told them of my desire, saying,
‘Do not invite me to such things!’

original:
Yo me kaniṭṭhako bhātā,
nando nāmāsi paṇḍito;
Sopi maṁ anusikkhanto,
pabbajjaṁ samarocayi.
text:
My younger brother,
who was named Nanda the astute,
followed my ethical practices,
and chose to go forth.

original:
Ahaṁ soṇo ca nando ca,
ubho mātāpitā mama;
Tadāpi bhoge chaḍḍetvā,
pāvisimhā mahāvanan”ti.
text:
I, Soṇa, and Nanda,
and both my mother and father,
then discarded our riches
and entered the great forest.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
kāsirājassa atrajo;
Mūgapakkhoti nāmena,
temiyoti vadanti maṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
the true-born son of the king of Kāsi,
Mūgapakkha was my name,
they called me Temiya.
title: Temiya’s Conduct (Temiyacariya)

original:
Soḷasitthisahassānaṁ,
na vijjati pumo tadā;
Ahorattānaṁ accayena,
nibbatto ahamekako.
text:
None of the sixteen thousand court women
had given birth to a male.
After many days and nights
I was born, the only one.

original:
Kicchā laddhaṁ piyaṁ puttaṁ,
abhijātaṁ jutindharaṁ;
Setacchattaṁ dhārayitvāna,
sayane poseti maṁ pitā.
text:
To my father I was a dear son born with difficulty,
a light-bringer of impeccable lineage.
Holding a white parasol over my bed,
my father provided for me.

original:
Niddāyamāno sayanavare,
Pabujjhitvānahaṁ tadā;
Addasaṁ paṇḍaraṁ chattaṁ,
Yenāhaṁ nirayaṁ gato.
text:
Sleeping on the fine bed,
then having awoken,
I saw the pale umbrella,
by which I had gone to hell.

original:
Saha diṭṭhassa me chattaṁ,
tāso uppajji bheravo;
Vinicchayaṁ samāpanno,
‘kathāhaṁ imaṁ muñcissaṁ’.
text:
At the sight of the umbrella
a terrible dread arose in me.
I reached the decision,
‘How can I be free of this?’

original:
Pubbasālohitā mayhaṁ,
devatā atthakāminī;
Sā maṁ disvāna dukkhitaṁ,
tīsu ṭhānesu yojayi.
text:
A former blood-relation of mine,
a goddess wishing to help,
saw my suffering
and enjoined me to three states.

original:
‘Mā paṇḍiccayaṁ vibhāvaya,
Bālamato bhava sabbapāṇinaṁ;
Sabbo taṁ jano ocināyatu,
Evaṁ tava attho bhavissati’.
text:
‘Don’t show intelligence,
be as a fool to all creatures,
let all folk scorn you,
thus you will achieve your goal.’

When she had spoken,
I said the following.
‘I shall do your bidding,
just as you say, goddess.
You want what’s best for me, mom,
you desire my welfare, goddess.’

original:
Tassāhaṁ vacanaṁ sutvā,
sāgareva thalaṁ labhiṁ;
Haṭṭho saṁviggamānaso,
tayo aṅge adhiṭṭhahiṁ.
text:
After hearing her words,
I was like one lost at sea reaching the shore.
I was thrilled, my mind elated,
and I resolved on three factors.

original:
Mūgo ahosiṁ badhiro,
pakkho gativivajjito;
Ete aṅge adhiṭṭhāya,
vassāni soḷasaṁ vasiṁ.
text:
I became deaf, and dumb,
and crippled, unable to walk.
Resolving on these factors,
I lived for sixteen years.

original:
Tato me hatthapāde ca,
jivhaṁ sotañca maddiya;
Anūnataṁ me passitvā,
‘kāḷakaṇṇī’ti nindisuṁ.
text:
Then they rubbed my hands and feet,
my tongue and ears as well,
and seeing no defect in me,
denounced me as ‘black-ear’.

original:
Tato jānapadā sabbe,
senāpatipurohitā;
Sabbe ekamanā hutvā,
chaḍḍanaṁ anumodisuṁ.
text:
Due to that, the entire country,
including the generals and priests,
with one mind
cheered as I was discarded.

original:
Sohaṁ tesaṁ matiṁ sutvā,
haṭṭho saṁviggamānaso;
‘Yassatthāya tapociṇṇo,
so me attho samijjhatha’.
text:
When I heard of their decision
I was thrilled, my mind elated,
‘The goal for which I lived fervently
I have achieved.’

original:
Nhāpetvā anulimpitvā,
veṭhetvā rājaveṭhanaṁ;
Chattena abhisiñcitvā,
kāresuṁ puraṁ padakkhiṇaṁ.
text:
Bathed and oiled,
with my turban wrapped,
anointed, they held the umbrella
as they paraded me around the city.

original:
Sattāhaṁ dhārayitvāna,
uggate ravimaṇḍale;
Rathena maṁ nīharitvā,
sārathī vanamupāgami.
text:
After the seventh day holding the umbrella,
when the sun’s orb had risen,
I was taken out by chariot,
until the charioteer came to a wood.

original:
Ekokāse rathaṁ katvā,
sajjassaṁ hatthamuccito;
Sārathī khaṇatī kāsuṁ,
nikhātuṁ pathaviyā mamaṁ.
text:
Leaving the chariot in the open,
the bridled horse released from his hand,
the charioteer dug a pit
to bury me in the ground.

original:
Adhiṭṭhitamadhiṭṭhānaṁ,
tajjento vividhakāraṇā;
Na bhindiṁ tamadhiṭṭhānaṁ,
bodhiyāyeva kāraṇā.
text:
I was afraid for the many different
resolves that I had undertaken,
so I did not break that resolve,
because it was solely for awakening.

original:
Mātāpitā na me dessā,
attā me na ca dessiyo;
Sabbaññutaṁ piyaṁ mayhaṁ,
tasmā vatamadhiṭṭhahiṁ.
text:
I had no dislike of my parents,
nor did I dislike myself.
But because omniscience is precious to me,
that is why I resolved on my vow.

original:
Ete aṅge adhiṭṭhāya,
Vassāni soḷasaṁ vasiṁ;
Adhiṭṭhānena me samo natthi,
Esā me adhiṭṭhānapāramī”ti.
text:
Having resolved the three factors,
I lived for sixteen years.
There is no one to equal my resolve:
this is my perfection of resolve.”

original:
“Yadā ahaṁ kapi āsiṁ,
nadīkūle darīsaye;
Pīḷito susumārena,
gamanaṁ na labhāmahaṁ.
text:
“When I was a monkey
in a cleft on the riverbank,
harassed by a crocodile
I could not get across.
title: The Monkey King’s Conduct (Kapirājacariya)

original:
Yamhokāse ahaṁ ṭhatvā,
orā pāraṁ patāmahaṁ;
Tatthacchi sattu vadhako,
kumbhīlo luddadassano.
text:
Where I used to land
when jumping from the near shore to the far,
there crouched my deadly foe,
the baleful gharial.

original:
So maṁ asaṁsi ‘ehī’ti,
‘ahampemī’ti taṁ vatiṁ;
Tassa matthakamakkamma,
parakūle patiṭṭhahiṁ.
text:
Reassuring me, he said ‘Come!’
‘I am coming,’ I said to him.
Stepping on his head
I made it to the far bank.

original:
Na tassa alikaṁ bhaṇitaṁ,
yathā vācaṁ akāsahaṁ;
Saccena me samo natthi,
esā me saccapāramī”ti.
text:
I spoke no lie to him,
but acted according to my word.
There is no one to equal my truthfulness:
this is my perfection of truth.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
Tāpaso saccasavhayo;
Saccena lokaṁ pālesiṁ,
Samaggaṁ janamakāsahan”ti.
text:
“Then again when I was
an ascetic known as Truthful,
I protected the world with my truth,
uniting the people.”
title: The Ascetic Truthful’s Conduct (Saccatāpasacariya)

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
magadhe vaṭṭapotako;
Ajātapakkho taruṇo,
maṁsapesi kulāvake.
text:
“Then again when I was
a baby quail in Magadha,
I was young, with wings unsprouted,
just a scrap of meat in the nest.
title: The Baby Quail’s Conduct (Vaṭṭapotakacariya)

original:
Mukhatuṇḍakenāharitvā,
mātā posayatī mamaṁ;
Tassā phassena jīvāmi,
natthi me kāyikaṁ balaṁ.
text:
With food she brought in her beak
my mother nurtured me.
I survived through her touch,
for I had no physical strength.

original:
Saṁvacchare gimhasamaye,
davaḍāho padippati;
Upagacchati amhākaṁ,
pāvako kaṇhavattanī.
text:
One year, in the hot season,
the forest caught fire.
It came toward us,
a conflagration with a blackened trail.

original:
Dhamadhamāiti evaṁ,
saddāyanto mahāsikhī;
Anupubbena jhāpento,
aggi mamamupāgami.
text:
The fire roared and rumbled
with great crests of flame,
gradually burning
closer to me.

original:
Aggivegabhayātītā,
tasitā mātāpitā mama;
Kulāvake maṁ chaḍḍetvā,
attānaṁ parimocayuṁ.
text:
Alarmed and terrified at the fierce fire,
my mother and father
abandoned me in the nest,
saving themselves.

original:
Pāde pakkhe pajahāmi,
natthi me kāyikaṁ balaṁ;
Sohaṁ agatiko tattha,
evaṁ cintesahaṁ tadā.
text:
I beat my feet and wings,
but I had no physical strength.
When unable to leave,
I thought this there:

original:
‘Yesāhaṁ upadhāveyyaṁ,
bhīto tasitavedhito;
Te maṁ ohāya pakkantā,
kathaṁ me ajja kātave.
text:
‘Those to whom I ought to run,
scared and trembling with fear,
have escaped, leaving me behind.
How should I act today?

original:
Atthi loke sīlaguṇo,
saccaṁ soceyyanuddayā;
Tena saccena kāhāmi,
saccakiriyamuttamaṁ.
text:
There is the quality of virtue in the world,
truth, purity, and mercy.
By this truth I will make
a supreme declaration of truth.’

original:
Āvejjetvā dhammabalaṁ,
saritvā pubbake jine;
Saccabalamavassāya,
saccakiriyamakāsahaṁ.
text:
Inspired by the power of Dhamma,
recollecting the former Victors,
relying on the power of truth,
I made a declaration of truth.

original:
Santi pakkhā apatanā,
santi pādā avañcanā;
Mātāpitā ca nikkhantā,
jātaveda paṭikkama’.
text:
‘I have wings that do not fly!
I have feet that do not walk!
Mother and father have fled!
Jātaveda the fire: go back!’

As I declared this truth
the great crested flames
withdrew sixteen leagues,
as if they had come to water.
There is no one to equal my truthfulness:
this is my perfection of truth.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
maccharājā mahāsare;
Uṇhe sūriyasantāpe,
sare udaka khīyatha.
text:
“Then again when I was
a fish king in a great lake,
in the heat of the sun
the water in the lake evaporated.
title: The Fish King’s Conduct (Maccharājacariya)

original:
Tato kākā ca gijjhā ca,
kaṅkā kulalasenakā;
Bhakkhayanti divārattiṁ,
macche upanisīdiya.
text:
Then crows and vultures,
herons, hawks, and falcons,
perched near the fish
and devoured them day and night.

original:
Evaṁ cintesahaṁ tattha,
saha ñātīhi pīḷito;
‘Kena nu kho upāyena,
ñātī dukkhā pamocaye’.
text:
There I had the following thought,
being harassed with my relatives:
‘By what means
can I free my relatives from this suffering?’

original:
Vicintayitvā dhammatthaṁ,
saccaṁ addasa passayaṁ;
Sacce ṭhatvā pamocesiṁ,
ñātīnaṁ taṁ atikkhayaṁ.
text:
Considering the value of the Dhamma,
I saw the truth as a support.
Standing in the truth,
I freed my relatives from that holocaust.

original:
Anussaritvā sataṁ dhammaṁ,
paramatthaṁ vicintayaṁ;
Akāsiṁ saccakiriyaṁ,
yaṁ loke dhuvasassataṁ.
text:
Recollecting the true Dhamma,
considered the ultimate goal,
I made a declaration of truth
that would last eternally in the world.

original:
‘Yato sarāmi attānaṁ,
yato pattosmi viññutaṁ;
Nābhijānāmi sañcicca,
ekapāṇampi hiṁsitaṁ.
text:
‘So long as I can recall myself,
since I became aware,
I do not recall deliberately
harming even a single living creature.

By this declaration of truth,
may Pajjuna rain down!
Thunder forth, Pajjuna!
Disperse the trove of the crow!
Subject the crow to sorrow,
and free the fish from sorrow!’

original:
Saha kate saccavare,
pajjunno abhigajjiya;
Thalaṁ ninnañca pūrento,
khaṇena abhivassatha.
text:
As this excellent truth was declared,
Pajjuna thundered forth.
In an instant the rain poured down,
soaking the uplands and valleys.

Having made such supreme effort
for this excellent truth,
I made the great cloud pour down,
relying on the force of the power of truth.
There is no one to equal my truthfulness:
this is my perfection of truth.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
kaṇhadīpāyano isi;
Paropaññāsavassāni,
anabhiratocariṁ ahaṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
the seer Dark Light,
for more than fifty years
I lived dissatisfied.
title: Dark Light’s Conduct (Kaṇhadīpāyanacariya)

original:
Na koci etaṁ jānāti,
Anabhiratimanaṁ mama;
Ahañhi kassaci nācikkhiṁ,
Arati me carati mānase.
text:
No one knew of this
dissatisfaction of mine,
for I mentioned it to no one,
it only went on in my mind.

original:
Sabrahmacārī maṇḍabyo,
sahāyo me mahāisi;
Pubbakammasamāyutto,
sūlamāropanaṁ labhi.
text:
Maṇḍabya, a spiritual companion
and friend of mine was a great seer.
Bound to a deed in a past life,
he got impaled on a stake.

original:
Tamahaṁ upaṭṭhahitvāna,
ārogyamanupāpayiṁ;
Āpucchitvāna āgañchiṁ,
yaṁ mayhaṁ sakamassamaṁ.
text:
I nursed him
and brought him back to health.
Asking leave, I returned
to my own hermitage.

original:
Sahāyo brāhmaṇo mayhaṁ,
bhariyaṁ ādāya puttakaṁ;
Tayo janā samāgantvā,
āgañchuṁ pāhunāgataṁ.
text:
A brahmin friend of mine,
bringing wife and child,
came to me, all three of them,
as my guests.

original:
Sammodamāno tehi saha,
nisinno sakamassame;
Dārako vaṭṭamanukkhipaṁ,
āsīvisamakopayi.
text:
As I exchanged greetings with them,
seated in my own hermitage,
the boy threw a ball
and angered a viper.

original:
Tato so vaṭṭagataṁ maggaṁ,
anvesanto kumārako;
Āsīvisassa hatthena,
uttamaṅgaṁ parāmasi.
text:
Then the boy, looking which way
the ball had gone,
touched the viper’s head
with his hand.

original:
Tassa āmasane kuddho,
sappo visabalassito;
Kupito paramakopena,
aḍaṁsi dārakaṁ khaṇe.
text:
Angered at his touch,
the cobra, relying on its potent poison,
completely enraged,
bit the boy right away.

original:
Sahadaṭṭho āsīvisena,
dārako papati bhūmiyaṁ;
Tenāhaṁ dukkhito āsiṁ,
mama vāhasi taṁ dukkhaṁ.
text:
When bitten by the viper,
the boy fainted on the ground.
It made me distraught,
the pain became as if mine.

original:
Tyāhaṁ assāsayitvāna,
dukkhite sokasallite;
Paṭhamaṁ akāsiṁ kiriyaṁ,
aggaṁ saccaṁ varuttamaṁ.
text:
Comforting the parents,
in their suffering and sorrow,
I made the first act,
the original, supreme declaration of truth:

original:
‘Sattāhamevāhaṁ pasannacitto,
Puññatthiko acariṁ brahmacariyaṁ;
Athāparaṁ yaṁ caritaṁ mamedaṁ,
Vassāni paññāsasamādhikāni.
text:
‘For just seven days with a mind of faith
I led the spiritual life seeking merit.
My life since then,
for fifty years or more,

I have lived unwillingly.
By this truth, may he be well!
May the poison die! May Yaññadatta live!’

As I declared this truth,
the boy trembling with poison,
awoke and got up,
the brahmin youth was well.
There is no one to equal my truthfulness:
this is my perfection of truth.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
sutasomo mahīpati;
Gahito porisādena,
brāhmaṇe saṅgaraṁ sariṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
Sutasoma, Lord of the Earth,
captured by a cannibal
I remembered my promise to a brahmin.
title: Sutasoma’s Conduct (Sutasomacariya)

original:
Khattiyānaṁ ekasataṁ,
āvuṇitvā karattale;
Etesaṁ pamilāpetvā,
yaññatthe upanayī mamaṁ.
text:
A hundred aristocrat warriors
he strung up by their hands.
Having drained their blood,
he brought me for sacrifice.

original:
Apucchi maṁ porisādo,
‘kiṁ tvaṁ icchasi nissajaṁ;
Yathāmati te kāhāmi,
yadi me tvaṁ punehisi’.
text:
The cannibal asked me,
‘What do you wish for—release?
I shall act as you think,
so long as you will return.’

original:
Tassa paṭissuṇitvāna,
paṇhe āgamanaṁ mama;
Upagantvā puraṁ rammaṁ,
rajjaṁ niyyādayiṁ tadā.
text:
I promised him that I
would return at dawn.
I went to the delightful city
and then renounced kingship.

original:
Anussaritvā sataṁ dhammaṁ,
pubbakaṁ jinasevitaṁ;
Brāhmaṇassa dhanaṁ datvā,
porisādaṁ upāgamiṁ.
text:
Recollecting the true Dhamma,
fostered by former Victors,
I gave money to the brahmin,
and returned to the cannibal.

I had no doubt
that he was going to kill me.
Protecting my truthful speech,
I went to give up my life.
There is no one to equal my truthfulness:
this is my perfection of truth.”

original:
“Sāmo yadā vane āsiṁ,
sakkena abhinimmito;
Pavane sīhabyagghe ca,
mettāya mupanāmayiṁ.
text:
“When in a wood I was Sāma the black,
created by Sakka.
I led the lions and tigers
in the forest by love.
title: Goldblack’s Conduct (Suvaṇṇasāmacariya)
