original:
Sīhabyagghehi dīpīhi,
acchehi mahisehi ca;
Pasadamigavarāhehi,
parivāretvā vane vasiṁ.
text:
Surrounded by lions and tigers,
leopards, bears, buffaloes,
spotted deer, and wild boar,
I stayed in the forest.

original:
Na maṁ koci uttasati,
napi bhāyāmi kassaci;
Mettābalenupatthaddho,
ramāmi pavane tadā”ti.
text:
None were scared of me,
nor I of them.
Sustained by the power of love
I delighted in the forest then.”

original:
“Punāparaṁ yadā homi,
ekarājāti vissuto;
Paramaṁ sīlaṁ adhiṭṭhāya,
pasāsāmi mahāmahiṁ.
text:
“Then again when I was
the renowned One King,
resolved on highest ethics,
I ruled the great earth.
title: The One King’s Conduct (Ekarājacariya)

original:
Dasa kusalakammapathe,
vattāmi anavasesato;
Catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi,
saṅgaṇhāmi mahājanaṁ.
text:
Without exception I followed
the ten ways of skillful deeds.
With the four ways of being inclusive,
I brought together the population.

original:
Evaṁ me appamattassa,
idha loke parattha ca;
Dabbaseno upagantvā,
acchindanto puraṁ mama.
text:
As I was being diligent,
for the sake of this world and the next,
Dabbasena attacked
and sacked my city.

original:
Rājūpajīve nigame,
sabalaṭṭhe saraṭṭhake;
Sabbaṁ hatthagataṁ katvā,
kāsuyā nikhaṇī mamaṁ.
text:
The royal dependents in the city,
with the military and the citizens—
he captured them all,
and buried me in a pit.

The court ministers, the flourishing kingdom,
and my royal court—
were captured and held,
I even saw my beloved son.
There is no one to equal my love:
this is my perfection of love.”

original:
“Susāne seyyaṁ kappemi,
Chavaṭṭhikaṁ upanidhāyahaṁ;
Gāmaṇḍalā upāgantvā,
Rūpaṁ dassentinappakaṁ.
text:
“I made my bed in a charnel ground,
resting on a skeleton.
Village louts came up
and mocked me in all sorts of ways.
title: The Great Hair-raising Conduct (Mahālomahaṁsacariya)

original:
Apare gandhamālañca,
bhojanaṁ vividhaṁ bahuṁ;
Upāyanānūpanenti,
haṭṭhā saṁviggamānasā.
text:
Others brought me
incense and flowers,
and many kinds of cooked food,
all thrilled, their minds elated.

original:
Ye me dukkhaṁ upaharanti,
ye ca denti sukhaṁ mama;
Sabbesaṁ samako homi,
dayā kopo na vijjati.
text:
Those who brought me pain,
and those who gave me happiness,
were all the same to me.
I felt no favor or anger.

original:
Sukhadukkhe tulābhūto,
Yasesu ayasesu ca;
Sabbattha samako homi,
Esā me upekkhāpāramī”ti.
text:
I became balanced toward pleasure and pain,
fame and disgrace.
I was equal in every case:
this is my perfection of equanimity.”

original:
Evaṁ bahubbidhaṁ dukkhaṁ,
sampattī ca bahubbidhā;
Bhavābhave anubhavitvā,
patto sambodhimuttamaṁ.
text:
Having thus experienced many kinds of suffering
and many kinds of success,
in various past lives,
I realized supreme awakening.

original:
Datvā dātabbakaṁ dānaṁ,
sīlaṁ pūretvā asesato;
Nekkhamme pāramiṁ gantvā,
patto sambodhimuttamaṁ.
text:
I gave what could be given,
and fulfilled ethics without reserve.
Having won the perfection of renunciation,
I realized supreme awakening.

original:
Paṇḍite paripucchitvā,
vīriyaṁ katvāna muttamaṁ;
Khantiyā pāramiṁ gantvā,
patto sambodhimuttamaṁ.
text:
I inquired of the astute,
and put forth highest effort,
having won the perfection of acceptance,
I realized supreme awakening.

original:
Katvā daḷhamadhiṭṭhānaṁ,
saccavācānurakkhiya;
Mettāya pāramiṁ gantvā,
patto sambodhimuttamaṁ.
text:
Having made a firm resolve,
and guarded truthful speech,
having won the perfection of love,
I realized supreme awakening.

original:
Lābhālābhe yasāyase,
sammānanāvamānane;
Sabbattha samako hutvā,
patto sambodhimuttamaṁ.
text:
In gain and loss, fame and disgrace,
respect and contempt,
having become equal in every case,
I realized supreme awakening.

original:
Kosajjaṁ bhayato disvā,
vīriyārambhañca khemato;
Āraddhavīriyā hotha,
esā buddhānusāsanī.
text:
Seeing laziness as fearful,
and energy as a sanctuary,
rouse up energy:
this is the Buddhas’ instruction!

original:
Vivādaṁ bhayato disvā,
avivādañca khemato;
Samaggā sakhilā hotha,
esā buddhānusāsanī.
text:
Seeing dispute as fearful,
and harmony as a sanctuary,
be harmonious and courteous:
this is the Buddhas’ instruction!

original:
Pamādaṁ bhayato disvā,
appamādañca khemato;
Bhāvethaṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ,
esā buddhānusāsanī.
text:
Seeing negligence as fearful,
and diligence as a sanctuary,
develop the eightfold path:
this is the Buddhas’ instruction!

original: Itthaṁ sudaṁ bhagavā attano pubbacariyaṁ sambhāvayamāno buddhāpadāniyaṁ nāma dhammapariyāyaṁ abhāsitthāti.
text: That is how the Buddha, illustrating his own conduct in past lives, spoke the exposition of the teaching named the “Legends of the Buddha”.
